Training Details\\\\nWe train a suite of models of various sizes in order to study\\\\nthe scaling properties of Whisper. Please see Table 1 for an\\\\noverview. We train with data parallelism across accelerators\\\\nusing FP16 with dynamic loss scaling and activation check-\\\\npointing (Griewank & Walther, 2000; Chen et al., 2016).\\\\nModels were trained with AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter,\\\\n2017) and gradient norm clipping (Pascanu et al., 2013)\\\\nwith a linear learning rate decay to zero after a warmup over\\\\nthe ﬁrst 2048 updates. A batch size of 256 segments was\\\\nused, and the models are trained for 220 updates which is\\\\nbetween two and three passes over the dataset. Due to only\\\\ntraining for a few epochs, over-ﬁtting is not a large concern,\\\\nand we do not use any data augmentation or regularization\\\\nand instead rely on the diversity contained within such a\\\\nlarge dataset to encourage generalization and robustness.\\\\nPlease see Appendix F for full training hyperparameters.3\\\\nDuring early development and evaluation we observed that\\\\nWhisper models had a tendency to transcribe plausible but\\\\nalmost always incorrect guesses for the names of speakers.\\\\nThis happens because many transcripts in the pre-training\\\\ndataset include the name of the person who is speaking,\\\\nencouraging the model to try to predict them, but this infor-\\\\nmation is only rarely inferable from only the most recent 30\\\\n3After the original release of Whisper, we trained an additional\\\\nLarge model (denoted V2) for 2.5X more epochs while adding\\\\nSpecAugment (Park et al., 2019), Stochastic Depth (Huang et al.,\\\\n2016), and BPE Dropout (Provilkov et al., 2019) for regularization.\\\\nReported results have been updated to this improved model unless\\\\notherwise speciﬁed.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 5 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n5\\\\nModel\\\\nLayers\\\\nWidth\\\\nHeads\\\\nParameters\\\\nTiny\\\\n4\\\\n384\\\\n6\\\\n39M\\\\nBase\\\\n6\\\\n512\\\\n8\\\\n74M\\\\nSmall\\\\n12\\\\n768\\\\n12\\\\n244M\\\\nMedium\\\\n24\\\\n1024\\\\n16\\\\n769M\\\\nLarge\\\\n32\\\\n1280\\\\n20\\\\n1550M\\\\nTable 1. To avoid this, we ﬁne-tune Whis-\\\\nper models brieﬂy on the subset of transcripts that do not\\\\ninclude speaker annotations which removes this behavior.\\\\n3. Experiments\\\\n3.1. Zero-shot Evaluation\\\\nThe goal of Whisper is to develop a single robust speech\\\\nprocessing system that works reliably without the need for\\\\ndataset speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning to achieve high-quality results\\\\non speciﬁc distributions. To study this capability, we re-\\\\nuse a wide set of existing speech processing datasets to\\\\ncheck whether Whisper is able to generalize well across\\\\ndomains, tasks, and languages. Instead of using the standard\\\\nevaluation protocol for these datasets, which include both\\\\na train and test split, we evaluate Whisper in a zero-shot\\\\nsetting without using any of the training data for each of\\\\nthese datasets so that we are measuring broad generalization.\\\\n3.2. Evaluation Metrics\\\\nSpeech recognition research typically evaluates and com-\\\\npares systems based on the word error rate (WER) metric.\\\\nHowever, WER, which is based on string edit distance, pe-\\\\nnalizes all differences between the model’s output and the\\\\nreference transcript including innocuous differences in tran-\\\\nscript style. As a result, systems that output transcripts that\\\\nwould be judged as correct by humans can still have a large\\\\nWER due to minor formatting differences. While this poses\\\\na problem for all transcribers, it is particularly acute for\\\\nzero-shot models like Whisper, which do not observe any\\\\nexamples of speciﬁc datasets transcript formats.\\\\nThis is not a novel observation; the development of evalua-\\\\ntion metrics that better correlate with human judgement is an\\\\nactive area of research, and while there are some promising\\\\nmethods, none have seen widespread adoption for speech\\\\nrecognition yet. We opt to address this problem with ex-\\\\ntensive standardization of text before the WER calculation\\\\nto minimize penalization of non-semantic differences. Our\\\\ntext normalizer was developed through iterative manual in-\\\\nspection to identify common patterns where naive WER\\\\npenalized Whisper models for an innocuous difference. Ap-\\\\npendix C includes full details. For several datasets, we\\\\nobserve WER drops of up to 50 percent usually due to a\\\\nquirk such as a dataset’s reference transcripts seperating\\\\ncontractions from words with whitespace. We caution this\\\\ndevelopment procedure comes at a risk of overﬁtting to the\\\\ntranscription style of Whisper models which we investigate\\\\nin Section 4.4. We are releasing the code for our text nor-\\\\nmalizer to allow for easy comparison and to help others\\\\nstudy the performance of speech recognition systems in\\\\nout-of-distribution settings.\\\\n3.3. English Speech Recognition\\\\nIn 2015, Deep Speech 2 (Amodei et al., 2015) reported\\\\na speech recognition system matched human-level perfor-\\\\nmance when transcribing the LibriSpeech test-clean split.\\\\nAs part of their analysis they concluded: “Given this result,\\\\nwe suspect that there is little room for a generic speech sys-\\\\ntem to further improve on clean read speech without further\\\\ndomain adaptation.” Yet seven years later the SOTA WER\\\\non LibriSpeech test-clean has dropped another 73% from\\\\ntheir 5.3% to 1.4% (Zhang et al., 2021), far below their re-\\\\nported human-level error rate of 5.8%. Despite this massive\\\\nand unanticipated further improvement in performance on\\\\nheld-out but in-distribution data, speech recognition mod-\\\\nels trained on LibriSpeech remain far above human error\\\\nrates when used in other settings. What explains this gap\\\\nbetween reportedly superhuman performance in-distribution\\\\nand subhuman performance out-of-distribution?\\\\nWe suspect a large part of this gap between human and\\\\nmachine behavior is due to conﬂating different capabilities\\\\nbeing measured by human and machine performance on\\\\na test set. This claim may seem confusing at ﬁrst; if both\\\\nhumans and machines are taking the same test, how can it be\\\\nthat different skills are being tested? The difference arises\\\\nnot in the testing but in how they trained for it. Humans are\\\\noften asked to perform a task given little to no supervision\\\\non the speciﬁc data distribution being studied. Thus human\\\\nperformance is a measure of out-of-distribution generaliza-\\\\ntion. But machine learning models are usually evaluated\\\\nafter training on a large amount of supervision from the\\\\nevaluation distribution, meaning that machine performance\\\\nis instead a measure of in-distribution generalization. While\\\\nboth humans and machines are being evaluated on the same\\\\ntest data, two quite different abilities are being measured\\\\ndue to a difference in train data.\\\\nWhisper models, which are trained on a broad and diverse\\\\ndistribution of audio and evaluated in a zero-shot setting,\\\\ncould potentially match human behavior much better than\\\\nexisting systems. To study whether this is the case (or\\\\nwhether the difference between machine and human per-\\\\nformance is due to yet-to-be-understood factors) we can\\\\ncompare Whisper models with both human performance\\\\nand standard ﬁne-tuned machine learning models and check\\\\nwhich they more closely match.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 6 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n6\\\\n0\\\\n1\\\\n2\\\\n3\\\\n4\\\\n5\\\\n6\\\\n7\\\\n8\\\\nWER on LibriSpeech dev-clean (%)\\\\n0\\\\n10\\\\n20\\\\n30\\\\n40\\\\n50\\\\nAverage WER on [Common Voice, CHiME-6, TED-LIUM] (%)\\\\nSupervised LibriSpeech models\\\\nZero-shot Whisper models\\\\nZero-shot Human (Alec)\\\\nIdeal robustness (y = x)\\\\nFigure 2. Despite matching or outperforming a human on Lib-\\\\nriSpeech dev-clean, supervised LibriSpeech models make roughly\\\\ntwice as many errors as a human on other datasets demonstrating\\\\ntheir brittleness and lack of robustness. The estimated robustness\\\\nfrontier of zero-shot Whisper models, however, includes the 95%\\\\nconﬁdence interval for this particular human.\\\\nTo quantify this difference, we examine both overall ro-\\\\nbustness, that is average performance across many distribu-\\\\ntions/datasets, and effective robustness, introduced by Taori\\\\net al. (2020), which measures the difference in expected\\\\nperformance between a reference dataset, which is usually\\\\nin-distribution, and one or more out-of-distribution datasets.\\\\nA model with high effective robustness does better than\\\\nexpected on out-of-distribution datasets as a function of its\\\\nperformance on the reference dataset and approaches the\\\\nideal of equal performance on all datasets. For our analy-\\\\nsis, we use LibriSpeech as the reference dataset due to its\\\\ncentral role in modern speech recognition research and the\\\\navailability of many released models trained on it, which\\\\nallows for characterizing robustness behaviors. We use a\\\\nsuite of 12 other academic speech recognition datasets to\\\\nstudy out-of-distribution behaviors. Full details about these\\\\ndatasets can be found in Appendix A.\\\\nOur main ﬁndings are summarized in Figure 2 and Table 2.\\\\nAlthough the best zero-shot Whisper model has a relatively\\\\nunremarkable LibriSpeech clean-test WER of 2.5, which\\\\nis roughly the performance of modern supervised baseline\\\\nor the mid-2019 state of the art, zero-shot Whisper models\\\\nhave very different robustness properties than supervised\\\\nLibriSpeech models and out-perform all benchmarked Lib-\\\\nriSpeech models by large amounts on other datasets. Robustness to Additive Noise\\\\nWe tested the noise robustness of Whisper models and 14\\\\nLibriSpeech-trained models by measuring the WER when\\\\neither white noise or pub noise from the Audio Degrada-\\\\ntion Toolbox (Mauch & Ewert, 2013) was added to the\\\\naudio. Long-form Transcription\\\\nWhisper models are trained on 30-second audio chunks and\\\\ncannot consume longer audio inputs at once. This is not a\\\\nproblem with most academic datasets comprised of short\\\\nutterances but presents challenges in real-world applications\\\\nwhich often require transcribing minutes- or hours-long au-\\\\ndio. We developed a strategy to perform buffered transcrip-\\\\ntion of long audio by consecutively transcribing 30-second\\\\nsegments of audio and shifting the window according to the\\\\ntimestamps predicted by the model. We observed that it\\\\nis crucial to have beam search and temperature scheduling\\\\nbased on the repetitiveness and the log probability of the\\\\nmodel predictions in order to reliably transcribe long audio.\\\\nThe full procedure is described in Section 4.5.\\\\nWe evaluate the long-form transcription performance on\\\\nseven datasets consisting of speech recordings of various\\\\nlengths and recording conditions, to cover as diverse a data\\\\ndistribution as possible. Full details about the long-form datasets can\\\\nbe found in Appendix A.\\\\nWe compare the performance with open-source models as\\\\nwell as 4 commercial ASR services. The results are sum-\\\\nmarized in Figure 6, showing the distribution of word error\\\\nrates from Whisper and the 4 commercial ASR services,\\\\nTED-LIUM3\\\\nMeanwhile\\\\nKincaid46\\\\nRev16\\\\nEarnings-21\\\\nEarnings-22\\\\nCORAAL\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\n35\\\\n40\\\\nWord Error Rate (%)\\\\nWhisper\\\\nCompany A\\\\nCompany B\\\\nCompany C\\\\nCompany D\\\\nNVIDIA STT (CTC large)\\\\nFigure 6. Comparison with Human Performance\\\\nBecause of ambiguous or indistinct speech as well as la-\\\\nbeling errors, there are different levels of irreducible error\\\\nin each dataset, and with WER metrics from ASR systems\\\\nalone it is difﬁcult to make sense of how much room for\\\\nimprovement exists in each dataset. To quantify how close\\\\nWhisper’s performance is to the human performance, we se-\\\\nlected 25 recordings from the Kincaid46 dataset and used 5\\\\nservices to obtain transcripts produced by professional tran-\\\\nscribers, among which one provides computer-assisted tran-\\\\nscription and the other four are entirely human-transcribed.\\\\nThe audio selection covers various recording conditions\\\\nsuch as scripted and unscripted broadcast, telephone and\\\\nVoIP calls, and meetings. Figure 7 shows the distribution\\\\nof per-example WERs and aggregate WER across the 25\\\\nrecordings, where the computer-assisted service has the\\\\nlowest aggregate WER that is 1.15% point better than Whis-\\\\nper’s, and the pure-human performance is only a fraction\\\\nof a percentage point better than Whisper’s. These results\\\\nindicate that Whisper’s English ASR performance is not\\\\nperfect but very close to human-level accuracy.\\\\n4. Analysis and Ablations\\\\n4.1. Model Scaling\\\\nA large amount of the promise in weakly supervised train-\\\\ning approaches is their potential to use datasets much larger\\\\nthan those in traditional supervised learning. However, this\\\\ncomes with the cost of using data that is possibly much\\\\nnoisier and lower quality than gold-standard supervision.\\\\nA concern with this approach is that although it may look\\\\npromising to begin with, the performance of models trained\\\\non this kind of data may saturate at the inherent quality level\\\\nof the dataset, which could be far below human level. A re-\\\\nlated concern is that as capacity and compute spent training\\\\non the dataset increases, models may learn to exploit the\\\\nWhisper\\\\nA\\\\nB\\\\nC\\\\nD\\\\nE\\\\nF\\\\nG\\\\nH\\\\nI\\\\n ASR \\\\n          \\\\n human transcription \\\\n \\\\n          computer-assisted\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\nWord Error Rate (%)\\\\nFigure 7. Strategies for Reliable Long-form Transcription\\\\nTranscribing long-form audio using Whisper relies on ac-\\\\ncurate prediction of the timestamp tokens to determine the\\\\namount to shift the model’s 30-second audio context win-\\\\ndow by, and inaccurate transcription in one window may\\\\nnegatively impact transcription in the subsequent windows.\\\\nWe have developed a set of heuristics that help avoid fail-\\\\nure cases of long-form transcription, which is applied in\\\\nthe results reported in sections 3.8 and 3.9. First, we use\\\\nbeam search with 5 beams using the log probability as the\\\\nscore function, to reduce repetition looping which happens\\\\nmore frequently in greedy decoding. We start with tem-\\\\nperature 0, i.e. always selecting the tokens with the high-\\\\nest probability, and increase the temperature by 0.2 up to\\\\n1.0 when either the average log probability over the gen-\\\\nerated tokens is lower than −1 or the generated text has a\\\\ngzip compression rate higher than 2.4. Providing the tran-\\\\nscribed text from the preceding window as previous-text\\\\nconditioning when the applied temperature is below 0.5\\\\nfurther improves the performance. We found that the proba-\\\\nbility of the <|nospeech|> token alone is not sufﬁcient\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 13 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n13\\\\nTED-LIUM3\\\\nMeanwhile\\\\nKincaid46\\\\nRev16\\\\nEarnings-21\\\\nEarnings-22\\\\nCORAAL\\\\nAverage\\\\nGreedy decoding only\\\\n3.95 5.16 9.69 11.7 10.7 14.0 22.0\\\\n11.0\\\\n+ Beam search\\\\n4.16 5.71 9.42 11.5 10.2 13.4 20.0\\\\n10.6\\\\n+ Temperature fallback\\\\n4.16 5.71 9.42 11.5 10.2 13.4 20.0\\\\n10.6\\\\n+ Voice activity detection\\\\n3.56 4.61 9.45 11.4 10.1 13.2 19.4\\\\n10.2\\\\n+ Previous text conditioning\\\\n3.42 6.16 8.72 11.0 9.63 13.3 18.1\\\\n10.0\\\\n+ Initial timestamp constraint\\\\n3.51 5.26 8.41 11.5 9.73 12.6 19.1\\\\n10.0\\\\nTable 7. Long-form transcription performance improves incremen-\\\\ntally as additional decoding heuristics are employed. Details on\\\\neach intervention are described in Section 4.5.\\\\nto distinguish a segment with no speech, but combining\\\\nthe no-speech probability threshold of 0.6 and the average\\\\nlog-probability threshold of −1 makes the voice activity\\\\ndetection of Whisper more reliable. Finally, to avoid a fail-\\\\nure mode where the model ignores the ﬁrst few words in\\\\nthe input, we constrained the initial timestamp token to be\\\\nbetween 0.0 and 1.0 second. Table 7 shows that adding each\\\\nof the interventions above incrementally reduces the WER\\\\noverall, but not evenly across the dataset. These heuristics\\\\nserve as a workaround for the noisy predictions of the model,\\\\nand more research would be needed to further improve the\\\\nreliability of long-form decoding.\\\\n5. Related Work\\\\nScaling Speech Recognition\\\\nA consistent theme across\\\\nspeech recognition research has been documenting the bene-\\\\nﬁts of scaling compute, models, and datasets. Early work ap-\\\\nplying deep learning to speech recognition found improved\\\\nperformance with model depth and size and leveraged GPU\\\\nacceleration to make training these larger models tractable\\\\n(Mohamed et al., 2009). Further research demonstrated that\\\\nthe beneﬁt of deep learning approaches to speech recogni-\\\\ntion increased with dataset size, improving from being only\\\\ncompetitive with prior GMM-HMM systems when using\\\\njust 3 hours of TIMIT training data for phone recognition\\\\nto achieving a 30% word error rate reduction when trained\\\\non the 2,000 hour Switchboard dataset (Seide et al., 2011).\\\\nLiao et al. (2013) is an early example of leveraging weakly\\\\nsupervised learning to increase the size of a deep learn-\\\\ning based speech recognition dataset by over 1,000 hours.\\\\nThese trends continued with Deep Speech 2 (Amodei et al.,\\\\n2015) being a notable system developing high-throughput\\\\ndistributed training across 16 GPUs and scaling to 12,000\\\\nhours of training data while demonstrating continuing im-\\\\nprovements at that scale. By leveraging semi-supervised\\\\npre-training, Narayanan et al. (2018) were able to grow\\\\ndataset size much further and study training on 162,000\\\\nhours of labeled audio. More recent work has explored\\\\nbillion-parameter models (Zhang et al., 2020) and using up\\\\nto 1,000,000 hours of training data (Zhang et al., 2021).\\\\nMultitask Learning\\\\nMultitask learning (Caruana, 1997)\\\\nhas been studied for a long time. In speech recognition,\\\\nmulti-lingual models have been explored for well over a\\\\ndecade (Schultz & Kirchhoff, 2006). An inspirational and\\\\nfoundational work in NLP exploring multi-task learning\\\\nwith a single model is Collobert et al. (2011). Multitask\\\\nlearning in the sequence-to-sequence framework (Sutskever\\\\net al., 2014) using multiple encoders and decoders was in-\\\\nvestigated in Luong et al. (2015). The use of language codes\\\\nwith a shared encoder/decoder architecture was ﬁrst demon-\\\\nstrated for machine translation by Johnson et al. (2017),\\\\nremoving the need for separate encoders and decoders. This\\\\napproach was simpliﬁed further into the “text-to-text” frame-\\\\nwork of McCann et al. (2018) and popularized by its success\\\\nwith large transformer language models in the work of Rad-\\\\nford et al. (2019) and Raffel et al. (2020). Toshniwal et al.\\\\n(2018) demonstrated jointly training a modern deep learn-\\\\ning speech recognition system on several languages with a\\\\nsingle model, and Pratap et al. (2020a) scaled this line of\\\\nwork signiﬁcantly to 50 languages with a billion-parameter\\\\nmodel. MUTE (Wang et al., 2020c) and mSLAM (Bapna\\\\net al., 2022) studied joint training over both text and speech\\\\nlanguage tasks, demonstrating transfer between them.\\\\nRobustness\\\\nThe question of how effectively models trans-\\\\nfer and how robust they are to distribution shift and other\\\\ntypes of perturbations has long been studied and is actively\\\\nbeing researched across many ﬁelds of machine learning.\\\\nTorralba & Efros (2011) highlighted the lack of generaliza-\\\\ntion of machine learning models between datasets over a\\\\ndecade ago. Many other works have shown and continu-\\\\nally reiterated how despite high performance on IID test\\\\nsets, machine learning models can still make many mistakes\\\\nwhen evaluated in even slightly different settings (Lake et al.,\\\\n2017; Jia & Liang, 2017; Alcorn et al., 2019; Barbu et al.,\\\\n2019; Recht et al., 2019). More recently, Taori et al. (2020)\\\\nstudied the robustness of image classiﬁcation models, and\\\\nMiller et al. (2020) investigated this for question-answering\\\\nmodels. A key ﬁnding has been that multi-domain train-\\\\ning increases robustness and generalization as discussed in\\\\nthe Introduction. This ﬁnding has been replicated across\\\\nmany ﬁelds in addition to speech recognition including NLP\\\\n(Hendrycks et al., 2020) and computer vision (Radford et al.,\\\\n2021).\\\\n6. Limitations and Future Work\\\\nFrom our experimental results, analyses, and ablations, we\\\\nhave noted several limitations and areas for future work.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 14 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n14\\\\nImproved decoding strategies.\\\\nAs we have scaled Whis-\\\\nper, we have observed that larger models have made steady\\\\nand reliable progress on reducing perception-related errors\\\\nsuch as confusing similar-sounding words. Many remaining\\\\nerrors, particularly in long-form transcription seem more\\\\nstubborn in nature and decidedly non-human/perceptual.\\\\nThey are a combination of failure modes of seq2seq mod-\\\\nels, language models, and text-audio alignment and include\\\\nproblems such as getting stuck in repeat loops, not tran-\\\\nscribing the ﬁrst or last few words of an audio segment, or\\\\ncomplete hallucination where the model will output a tran-\\\\nscript entirely unrelated to the actual audio. Although the\\\\ndecoding details discussed in Section 4.5 help signiﬁcantly,\\\\nwe suspect ﬁne-tuning Whisper models on a high-quality\\\\nsupervised dataset and/or using reinforcement learning to\\\\nmore directly optimize for decoding performance could help\\\\nfurther reduce these errors.\\\\nIncrease Training Data For Lower-Resource Languages\\\\nAs Figure 3 shows, Whisper’s speech recognition perfor-\\\\nmance is still quite poor on many languages. The same\\\\nanalysis suggests a clear route for improvement since perfor-\\\\nmance on a language is very well predicted by the amount\\\\nof training data for the language. Since our pre-training\\\\ndataset is currently very English-heavy due to biases of\\\\nour data collection pipeline, which sourced primarily from\\\\nEnglish-centric parts of the internet, most languages have\\\\nless than 1000 hours of training data. A targeted effort at in-\\\\ncreasing the amount of data for these rarer languages could\\\\nresult in a large improvement to average speech recognition\\\\nperformance even with only a small increase in our overall\\\\ntraining dataset size.\\\\nStudying ﬁne-tuning\\\\nIn this work, we have focused on\\\\nthe robustness properties of speech processing systems and\\\\nas a result only studied the zero-shot transfer performance\\\\nof Whisper. While this is a crucial setting to study due to it\\\\nbeing representative of general reliability, for many domains\\\\nwhere high-quality supervised speech data does exist, it is\\\\nlikely that results can be improved further by ﬁne-tuning.\\\\nAn additional beneﬁt of studying ﬁne-tuning is that it allows\\\\nfor direct comparisons with prior work since it is a much\\\\nmore common evaluation setting.\\\\nStudying the impact of Language Models on Robustness\\\\nAs argued in the introduction, we suspect that Whisper’s\\\\nrobustness is partially due to its strong decoder, which is an\\\\naudio conditional language model. It’s currently unclear to\\\\nwhat degree the beneﬁts of Whisper stem from training its\\\\nencoder, decoder, or both. This could be studied by either\\\\nablating various design components of Whisper, such as\\\\ntraining a decoder-less CTC model, or by studying how the\\\\nperformance of existing speech recognition encoders such\\\\nas wav2vec 2.0 change when used together with a language\\\\nmodel.\\\\nAdding Auxiliary Training Objectives\\\\nWhisper departs\\\\nnoticeably from most recent state-of-the-art speech recog-\\\\nnition systems due to the lack of unsupervised pre-training\\\\nor self-teaching methods. While we have not found them\\\\nnecessary to achieve good performance, it is possible that\\\\nthe results could be further improved by incorporating this.\\\\n7. Conclusion\\\\nWhisper suggests that scaling weakly supervised pre-\\\\ntraining has been underappreciated so far in speech recogni-\\\\ntion research. We achieve our results without the need for\\\\nthe self-supervision and self-training techniques that have\\\\nbeen a mainstay of recent large-scale speech recognition\\\\nwork and demonstrate how simply training on a large and\\\\ndiverse supervised dataset and focusing on zero-shot trans-\\\\nfer can signiﬁcantly improve the robustness of a speech\\\\nrecognition system.\\\\nACKNOWLEDGMENTS\\\\nWe’d like to thank the millions of people who were involved\\\\nin creating the data used by Whisper. Text Standardization\\\\nSince Whisper may output any UTF-8 string rather than a restricted set of graphemes, the rules for text standardization need\\\\nto be more intricate and comprehensive than those deﬁned on e.g. ASCII characters. We perform the following steps to\\\\nnormalize English texts in different styles into a standardized form, which is a best-effort attempt to penalize only when a\\\\nword error is caused by actually mistranscribing a word, and not by formatting or punctuation differences.\\\\n1. Remove any phrases between matching brackets ([, ]).\\\\n2. Remove any phrases between matching parentheses ((, )).\\\\n3. Remove any of the following words: hmm, mm, mhm, mmm, uh, um\\\\n4. Remove whitespace characters that comes before an apostrophe ’\\\\n5. Convert standard or informal contracted forms of English into the original form.\\\\n6. Remove commas (,) between digits\\\\n7. Remove periods (.) not followed by numbers\\\\n8. Remove symbols as well as diacritics from the text, where symbols are the characters with the Unicode category\\\\nstarting with M, S, or P, except period, percent, and currency symbols that may be detected in the next step.\\\\n9. Detect any numeric expressions of numbers and currencies and replace with a form using Arabic numbers, e.g. “Ten\\\\nthousand dollars” →“$10000”.\\\\n10. Convert British spellings into American spellings.\\\\n11. Remove remaining symbols that are not part of any numeric expressions.\\\\n12. Replace any successive whitespace characters with a space.\\\\nA different, language-speciﬁc set of transformations would be needed to equivalently normalize non-English text, but due to\\\\nour lack of linguistic knowledge to build such normalizers for all languages, we resort to the following basic standardization\\\\nfor non-English text:\\\\n1. Remove any phrases between matching brackets ([, ]).\\\\n2. Remove any phrases between matching parentheses ((, )).\\\\n3. Replace any markers, symbols, and punctuation characters with a space, i.e. when the Unicode category of each\\\\ncharacter in the NFKC-normalized string starts with M, S, or P.\\\\n4. make the text lowercase.\\\\n5. replace any successive whitespace characters with a space.\\\\nAdditionally, we put a space between every letter for the languages that do not use spaces to separate words, namely Chinese,\\\\nJapanese, Thai, Lao, and Burmese, effectively measuring the character error rate instead.\\\\nWe note that the above is an imperfect solution, and it will sometimes produce unintended and unexpected outputs. We do\\\\nnot claim that the text format resulting from the above is more “correct” in any measure. Rather, the procedures above are\\\\ndesigned to better distinguish between innocuous differences in wording and genuine mistranscriptions. Python code for\\\\nthe standardization procedures above is available as part of our code and model release to facilitate future iterations and\\\\nimprovements on text standardization.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 22 ---\\\\nRobust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision\\\\n22\\\\nD. Moon-\\\\nshine is based on an encoder-decoder transformer\\\\narchitecture and employs Rotary Position Em-\\\\nbedding (RoPE) instead of traditional absolute\\\\nposition embeddings. The model is trained on\\\\nspeech segments of various lengths, but with-\\\\nout using zero-padding, leading to greater ef-\\\\nficiency for the encoder during inference time.\\\\nWhen benchmarked against OpenAI’s Whisper\\\\ntiny.en, Moonshine Tiny demonstrates a 5x re-\\\\nduction in compute requirements for transcribing\\\\na 10-second speech segment while incurring no in-\\\\ncrease in word error rates across standard evalua-\\\\ntion datasets. These results highlight Moonshine’s\\\\npotential for real-time and resource-constrained\\\\napplications.\\\\n1. Introduction\\\\nReal-time automatic speech recognition (ASR) is essential\\\\nfor many applications, including live transcription during\\\\npresentations, accessibility tools for individuals with hear-\\\\ning impairments, and voice command processing for conver-\\\\nsational interfaces in smart devices and wearables. These\\\\napplications often run directly on low-cost hardware, where\\\\nstrict resource constraints and a lack of internet connectivity\\\\nintroduce unique technical challenges that are not present in\\\\nother ASR domains.\\\\nThe introduction of OpenAI’s Whisper has led to a signifi-\\\\ncant improvement in the accuracy of general-purpose ASR\\\\nsystems (Radford et al., 2022). However, one of the pri-\\\\nmary challenges in applications of on-device ASR is the\\\\nneed to minimize latency—the time delay between a spoken\\\\nutterance and the corresponding text appearing, e.g., on a\\\\nlive transcription display—without losing accuracy. During\\\\n.\\\\nCorrespondence\\\\nto:\\\\nManjunath\\\\nKudlur\\\\n<keve-\\\\nman@usefulsensors.com>.\\\\nour development of one such application—a Caption Box\\\\nbuilt to provide rapid, accurate, and private offline transcrip-\\\\ntion of English speech—we found that current models are\\\\nill-suited to the task. When deployed on a low-cost ARM-\\\\nbased processor, we noticed that even the smallest Whisper\\\\ntiny.en model had a firm lower latency bound of 500\\\\nmilliseconds, irrespective of the duration of audio. User\\\\nfeedback indicated that this level of latency failed to provide\\\\na smooth and responsive user experience, which motivated\\\\nus to investigate deeper.\\\\nWhisper, which is based on an encoder-decoder transformer\\\\narchitecture, processes fixed-length audio sequences in 30-\\\\nsecond chunks regardless of the actual speech content of\\\\nthe audio. This means that shorter audio sequences require\\\\npadding with zeros to meet the length requirement, resulting\\\\nin a constant computational overhead in the encoder. While\\\\nthe decoder’s processing time is proportional to the length\\\\nof the utterance, the constant overhead of fixed-length en-\\\\ncoding places a firm lower bound to latency—e.g., the 500\\\\nmilliseconds we identified during our own testing with the\\\\nCaption Box. Our initial attempts to remove this bottle-\\\\nneck involved fine-tuning and distilling 1 Whisper models\\\\nto handle variable-length sequences in the encoder, utilizing\\\\nopen audio datasets. However, these open datasets proved\\\\ninsufficient to surpass Whisper’s Word Error Rate (WER).\\\\nRecognizing the limits of available data and the opportunity\\\\nto leverage recent advancements in model architectures, we\\\\nopted to develop and train new models from scratch.\\\\nOur first task was to better quantify the bottleneck imposed\\\\nby Whisper’s fixed-length encoder. In an empirical test,\\\\nwe compared the GFLOPS (i.e., billion floating-point op-\\\\nerations) needed for processing 30 seconds of zero-padded\\\\naudio to the GFLOPS that would be required to instead pro-\\\\ncess only a < 30 second subset of the same audio—i.e., we\\\\nmeasured the potential for speed-ups if Whisper instead had\\\\na variable-length encoder. Our results (Figure 1) showed\\\\npotential for a 35x speed-up in the best case, and nearly a\\\\n5x speed-up overall. Clearly, improvements to Whisper’s\\\\narchitecture could yield lightweight, low-latency speech-to-\\\\n1Hence the name Moonshine. We progressed to not use distil-\\\\nlation eventually, but the name stuck.\\\\narXiv:2410.15608v2  [cs.SD]  22 Oct 2024\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 2 ---\\\\nMoonshine: Speech Recognition for Live Transcription and Voice Commands\\\\n2\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\nAbsolute\\\\nFixed-length encoder\\\\nVariable-length encoder\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\nSeconds of audio\\\\n2x\\\\n5x\\\\n10x\\\\n20x\\\\n40x\\\\nSpeed-up (log scale)\\\\nVariable-length encoder\\\\nGFLOPS to decode\\\\nFigure 1. GFLOPS required by Whisper tiny.en for decoding\\\\nas a function of input audio duration. OpenAI’s Whisper models\\\\nuse a fixed-length encoder that requires any audio less than 30\\\\nseconds to be zero-padded; testing with a hypothetical variable-\\\\nlength encoder shows that we can attain significant speed-ups by\\\\nremoving this requirement.\\\\ntext models that are better-suited to resource-constrained\\\\napplications.\\\\nToward tackling the challenges faced by on-device, low-\\\\nlatency ASR applications, this paper introduces the Moon-\\\\nshine family of ASR models. Moonshine models are de-\\\\nsigned to match Whisper’s accuracy while optimizing com-\\\\nputational efficiency by eliminating zero-padding require-\\\\nments, instead scaling processing demands proportionally\\\\nto audio input length. We describe Moonshine’s architec-\\\\nture and training process, and provide a detailed analysis\\\\nof its performance benefits in comparison with Whisper\\\\nmodels. Section 2 motivates our development of Moon-\\\\nshine by quantifying the WER when adapting Whisper for\\\\nvariable-length audio. Section 3 describes the Moonshine\\\\narchitecture, dataset preparation, and training process, while\\\\nSection 4 provides an evaluation of the results on standard\\\\nspeech recognition datasets. Section 5 concludes.\\\\n2. Issues with fixed sequence length encoder\\\\nWhisper models use absolute position embeddings in both\\\\nthe encoder and decoder. The encoder in particular uses\\\\nsinusoidal position embeddings of shape [1500, dim],\\\\nwhere dim is the transformer encoder’s dimension. The\\\\nstandard inference code provided by OpenAI zero-pads the\\\\ninput audio to an exact 30-second segment before passing it\\\\ndown to the model. Audio feature generation and 2 convolu-\\\\ntion layers convert this audio segment to a [1500, dim]\\\\nvector sequence that gets added to the sinusoidal position\\\\nembedding. The left-most column of Figure 2 illustrates\\\\nthis mechanism.\\\\nRequiring an exact 30-second segment causes the encoder\\\\nto incur a fixed computation cost, no matter the duration\\\\nof actual speech in the audio segment. However, since\\\\nWhisper’s model architecture is an off-the-shelf, variable-\\\\nlength sequence-to-sequence transformer, zero-padding is\\\\nnot strictly necessary. An audio segment that is shorter\\\\nthan 30 seconds can indeed be processed through the\\\\nmodel’s frontend to yield a [seq_length, dim] vector\\\\nsequence where seq_length <= 1500.\\\\nThere are several options for adding the position embedding\\\\nto a variable-length audio input. We compared the default\\\\nimplementation in OpenAI’s Whisper inference code (i.e.,\\\\nusing zero-padding to form 30-second segments) with two\\\\nother options, as illustrated in the center and right-most\\\\ncolumns of Figure 2—namely, using the prefix and the\\\\nsuffix of the position embedding. We computed the WER\\\\nfor the tiny.en model using these two options on the\\\\ntest.clean split of the Librispeech dataset. This split\\\\nhas 2620 examples, 9 of which are more than 30 seconds in\\\\nlength. We ignore these 9 examples in this evaluation. We\\\\nuse a beam size of 5, so as to not suffer the pitfalls of greedy\\\\ndecoding such as repetitions. With the standard inference\\\\ncode provided by OpenAI, we get a WER of 5.21%. When\\\\nthe input is not zero-padded, however, we get worse results.\\\\nWhen using only a prefix of the position embedding, the\\\\ntiny.en model has a WER of 107.38%. We notice a\\\\nlot of repetitions towards the end of the transcription, even\\\\nwith the beam search. When instead using the suffix of\\\\nthe position embedding, the accuracy degradation is not as\\\\ndramatic, producing a WER of 18.45%—still more than\\\\nthree times worse than the baseline.\\\\nThese results indicate that the OpenAI Whisper models\\\\nare trained with examples that are all exactly 30 seconds\\\\nlong. The models indeed produce high quality transcrip-\\\\ntions for long-form audio. However, the fixed computation\\\\nbudget needed for their encoder makes them inefficient for\\\\nlow-latency applications, such as live transcription. Since\\\\nthe audio segments in these applications tend to be short\\\\nand/or vary in length, our effort to train models optimized\\\\nfor variable-length sequences is well-motivated.\\\\n3. Approach\\\\nThis section describes Moonshine’s model architecture be-\\\\nfore detailing our data collection, preprocessing, and model\\\\ntraining process.\\\\n3.1. Model architecture\\\\nMoonshine is an off-the-shelf encoder-decoder Transformer\\\\n(Vaswani et al., 2017) model. The input is an audio signal\\\\nsampled at 16,000 Hz. We do not use any hand-engineering\\\\n(e.g., Mel spectrograms) to extract audio features. Instead,\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 3 ---\\\\nMoonshine: Speech Recognition for Live Transcription and Voice Commands\\\\n3\\\\nx + positional_embedding[:,:]\\\\nx + positional_embedding[:x.shape[1],:]\\\\nx + positional_embedding[-x.shape[1]:,:]\\\\n+\\\\n+\\\\n+\\\\n5.21% WER\\\\n107.38% WER\\\\n18.45% WER\\\\nZero-Padded\\\\nTruncated (Prefix)\\\\nTruncated (Suffix)\\\\nFigure 2. Variations of absolute position embeddings usage and the corresponding WER produced by Whisper tiny.en (test.clean\\\\nsplit of the Librispeech dataset). Simply adapting Whisper’s inference code to avoid encoding of fixed-length audio (as in the center and\\\\nright-most columns) introduces significant increases in WER, motivating our development of new models with variable-length encoding.\\\\nthe input is processed by a short stem of 3 convolution layers\\\\nwith strides 64, 3, and 2 respectively. The filter widths,\\\\nnumber of channels and activation functions are shown in\\\\nFigure 3. These set of strides compress the input by a\\\\nfactor of 384x. Note that in the Whisper model, the input is\\\\ncompressed by 320x—firstly 160x in the Mel spectogram\\\\ncomputation, then by a further 2x in the convolution stem.\\\\nWe use Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) (Su et al., 2023)\\\\nat each layer of the encoder and decoder. The original vocabulary size is\\\\n32000; we add 768 special tokens for future extensions.\\\\n3.2. Training data collection & preprocessing\\\\nWe train Moonshine on a combination of 90K hours\\\\nfrom open ASR datasets and over 100K hours from own\\\\ninternally-prepared dataset, totalling around 200K hours.\\\\nFrom open datasets, we use Common Voice 16.1 (Ardila\\\\net al., 2020), the AMI corpus (Carletta et al., 2005), Gi-\\\\ngaSpeech (Chen et al., 2021), LibriSpeech (Panayotov\\\\net al., 2015), the English subset of multilingual Lib-\\\\nriSpeech (Pratap et al., 2020), and People’s Speech (Galvez\\\\net al., 2021). We then augment this training corpus with\\\\ndata that we collect from openly-available sources on the\\\\nweb. We discuss preparation methods for our self-collected\\\\ndata in the following.\\\\nPreprocessing noisily-labeled speech.\\\\nMany speech\\\\nsources available on the web have subtitles or captions avail-\\\\nable, which can serve as labels. However, captions tend be\\\\nnoisy—they may be manually-generated and thus contain\\\\ntext that is orthogonal to the audio content, or they may\\\\ncontain the names of speakers or verbal descriptions of non-\\\\nspeech content. In cases where a manually-generated but\\\\npossibly-unreliable caption is available, we use a heuristic\\\\nprocess to filter out low-quality instances. First, we lower-\\\\ncase and normalize the caption text, removing or replacing,\\\\ne.g., ambiguous unicode characters, emoji, and punctuation.\\\\nWe then use Whisper large v3 to generate a pseudo-label\\\\nof the audio content, applying the same text normalization\\\\nto this pseudo-label as we do the caption. Finally, we com-\\\\npute a normalized Levenshtein distance (between [0.0, 1.0],\\\\nwhere 0.0 is identical and 1.0 is orthogonal) between the\\\\nnormalized caption and the pseudo-label, filtering out labels\\\\nwith a distance above a threshold. This allows us to treat the\\\\nhuman-generated labels in captions as ground truth without\\\\nintroducing excessive noise. After filtering out noisy labels,\\\\nwe prepare the remaining text by applying standardized\\\\npunctuation and capitalization.\\\\nPreprocessing unlabeled speech. The majority of speech\\\\navailable on the web is unlabeled. In these cases, we lever-\\\\nage the Whisper large v3 model to generate training labels\\\\nfor our lighter-weight Moonshine model. The risk inherent\\\\nin training one model on another model’s outputs is that\\\\nthe new model learns the old model’s errors. From inspec-\\\\ntion, we noted that the majority of hallucinated outputs from\\\\nWhisper large v3 occurred below a predictable value of the\\\\naverage log probability of the output. We thus mitigate\\\\nthe risk of introducing hallucination and other noise in the\\\\ntraining set by filtering out instances with an average log\\\\nprobability below this threshold. During this process, we\\\\nbenefited from speed-ups provided by batched inference in\\\\nthe WhisperX implementation (Bain et al., 2023).\\\\nControlling instance duration. We assemble successive\\\\nspeech segments into longer training instances, such that\\\\nthe resulting instance duration is ∈[4, 30] seconds with no\\\\nmore than 2 seconds between successive segments. For\\\\nour manually-captioned data sources, we use timestamped\\\\nsegments provided by a subtitle file (e.g., an .srt file); for\\\\nour pseudo-labeled audio, we use the timestamps output by\\\\nWhisper. Upon combining this data with open datasets, the\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 4 ---\\\\nMoonshine: Speech Recognition for Live Transcription and Voice Commands\\\\n4\\\\nRoPE\\\\nself-attention\\\\nFFN + GELU\\\\nFFN + SwiGLU\\\\nRoPE\\\\nself-attention\\\\ncross-attention\\\\n...\\\\nConv1D\\\\ntanh\\\\nkernel size: 127\\\\nstride: 64\\\\nConv1D\\\\nGELU\\\\nkernel size: 7\\\\nstride: 3\\\\n...\\\\nConv1D\\\\nkernel size: 3\\\\nstride: 2\\\\nEncoder\\\\nBlocks\\\\nDecoder\\\\nBlocks\\\\nnext-token\\\\nprediction\\\\nBPE\\\\nGELU\\\\nFigure 3. Training\\\\nWe performed training on a 32x H100 GPU cluster, using\\\\nGPU data parallelism provided by Huggingface’s Accel-\\\\nerate library (Gugger et al., 2022). We used Accelerate’s\\\\nBF16 mixed precision optimizations. We trained the mod-\\\\nels for 250K steps with a batch size of 32 per GPU (1024\\\\nglobal batch size). Accuracy vs. Input Length\\\\nMoonshine models demonstrate the ability to transcribe\\\\naudio clips of varying lengths. However, we hypothesize\\\\nthat shorter inputs may result in higher WER due to the lack\\\\nof sufficient contextual information. Conversely, for longer\\\\nclips—particularly those exceeding the sequence lengths\\\\nobserved during training—there is a notable increase in\\\\ntranscription errors due to hallucinations. To evaluate this\\\\nbehavior, we measured the WER across a range of audio\\\\nsegments from the TEDLium dataset, with clip durations\\\\nvarying between 10 and 55 seconds.\\\\nTo evaluate inference speed across different clip lengths,\\\\nwe compare Moonshine and Whisper on GPU (H100). The\\\\nresults are depicted in Figure 5. The speed-up comparison\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 6 ---\\\\nMoonshine: Speech Recognition for Live Transcription and Voice Commands\\\\n6\\\\n60\\\\n50\\\\n40\\\\n30\\\\n20\\\\n10\\\\n0\\\\n10\\\\nLinear Gain (dB)\\\\n3%\\\\n5%\\\\n10%\\\\n20%\\\\n40%\\\\nWER\\\\nMoonshine Base\\\\nWhisper base.en\\\\n0\\\\n5\\\\n10\\\\n15\\\\n20\\\\n25\\\\n30\\\\nSNR (dB)\\\\n3%\\\\n5%\\\\n10%\\\\n20%\\\\n40%\\\\nWER\\\\nFigure 6. Robustness to Input Speech Signal Level\\\\nDuring this work, we observed that the robustness of Whis-\\\\nper models varies relative to the level of the input speech\\\\nsignal. To measure the impact of input levels (i.e., linear\\\\ngain) on Moonshine, we tested model robustness as increas-\\\\ning gain is applied to the audio samples in the dataset. As\\\\nshown in the left portion of Figure 6, Moonshine Base main-\\\\ntains superior WER over most of this range until the input\\\\nspeech signal is very attenuated. At this point (where gain\\\\nis below -40 dB, i.e., the input audio is very quiet) the WER\\\\nrises above the Whisper model. For practical applications\\\\nwhere high speech attenuation can be avoided in system\\\\ndesign, Moonshine Base is robust to varying input levels.\\\\n4.3. Robustness to Additive Noise\\\\nWe tested the noise robustness of the Moonshine Base model\\\\nby measuring the WER for the fan noise observed in a tablet\\\\ncomputer application under load. In user studies, we quanti-\\\\nfied the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for this application in\\\\nthe range [9, 17] dB depending on the speaker. We calculate\\\\nthe level of additive noise corresponding to a given SNR\\\\nbased on the average signal power of individual dataset ex-\\\\namples with quiet sections removed. The right portion of\\\\nFigure 6 shows how the performance degrades as fan noise\\\\nincreases. Whisper’s robustness to noise is known (Radford\\\\net al., 2022); Moonshine Base maintains this robustness\\\\nwhile providing a superior WER.\\\\n5. Discussion & Conclusion\\\\nWe briefly discuss limitations before concluding the paper\\\\nin this section.\\\\nArchitectures and optimizers.\\\\nAs in any research of\\\\nthis kind, many variations of model architecture could be\\\\nexplored. Likewise, recent advancements in optimizers—\\\\nparticularly Shampoo (Gupta et al., 2018) and SOAP (Vyas\\\\net al., 2024)—show promise for improving WERs in our\\\\narchitecture. Conducting an ablation study on these model\\\\narchitectures and training methods would significantly en-\\\\nhance the community’s understanding of the models’ limi-\\\\ntations. However, due to resource constraints, particularly\\\\nlimited affordability of GPUs, such studies are beyond the\\\\nscope of this paper. Consequently, we chose our architec-\\\\nture and optimizer based on the authors’ experience and a\\\\nthorough review of relevant literature.\\\\nGeneralization to shorter audio segments. The relatively\\\\nlow performance that we observed on the Earnings22 dataset\\\\nmotivates collection of more data representative of this case,\\\\nand investigation of training techniques to introduce more\\\\ncontextual information in the model. This will likely im-\\\\nprove model performance with no changes to architecture.\\\\nIn this paper we introduced Moonshine, a family of\\\\nlightweight ASR models optimized for low latency, on-\\\\ndevice speech-to-text applications. We outlined our model\\\\narchitecture, data collection and preprocessing procedures,\\\\nand training. We benchmarked Moonshine against two\\\\nOpenAI Whisper models—tiny.en and base.en—\\\\nshowing that their Moonshine counterparts provide up to 3x\\\\nreductions in latency scaled to the duration of input audio.\\\\nOur work opens the door for new applications of real-time\\\\nASR in live transcription, accessibility technologies, and\\\\nsmart devices.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 7 ---\\\\nMoonshine: Speech Recognition for Live Transcription and Voice Commands\\\\n7\\\\n6. K-MODEL-005：Encoder-decoder：源表示、两套 Attention 与流式边界\\\\n\\\\nEncoder-decoder 不是把同一套 causal attention 跑两遍，而是把源编码与目标生成分成两个有依赖的阶段：源表示支持固定复用，目标生成按自回归推进，流式输入又让源表示可能更新。本章把源表示、两套 attention、cross KV 复用条件、块边界与提交状态放在同一条数据流上。\\\\n\\\\n## 对象、函数与状态\\\\n\\\\n设一次请求含音频或文本源 A、请求身份 r、采样率、声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、模型权重版本和任务 token。processor 把 A 变成特征 X∈R^{F×d_in}，并给出有效位置与 padding；encoder 产生源表示 E∈R^{S×d_e}。这里 S 是模型的实际源位置数，不一定等于音频采样点数或网络包数。decoder 已消费的目标前缀为 y_{<t}，第 t 步隐藏状态为 H_t。\\\\n\\\\n对第 l 层 cross-attention，令 K_l＝E·W^K_l、V_l＝E·W^V_l、Q_t＝H_t·W^Q_l，则可见源集合 M_cross 下的输出为 A_{l,t}＝softmax(Q_t K_l^T／√d_h＋M_cross)·V_l。decoder self-attention 的 K/V 来自目标历史，可见集合 M_self 只允许当前位置及之前的目标位置；encoder self-attention 的可见性由模型定义，常见离线模型可在有效源内双向，但这不是所有流式模型的承诺。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态至少包含：源版本 v、源有效长度 S、E 或各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、已计算目标位置 t、已提交稳定文本前缀、已消费源样本偏移、已发布样本或时间戳边界、暂定输出和取消代次。状态要区分已计算、已验证、已发布和已回收，不能把“模型算出 token”直接当成“用户已看到稳定文字”。\\\\n\\\\n## 三类可见性与合法性\\\\n\\\\n| attention | Q 的来源 | K/V 的来源 | 典型可见性 | 状态变化 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| encoder self | encoder 当前层 | encoder 当前层 | 由模型定义，可双向或分块 | 固定源时一次算完；流式源可能重算 |\\\\n| decoder self | decoder 当前层 | 已生成目标前缀 | 通常因果，不得看未来目标 token | 每步追加，长度随目标增长 |\\\\n| cross | decoder 当前层 | encoder 源表示 | 由任务和模型定义；流式只可看已提交源或明确 lookahead | 源固定时只读，源更新时可追加、替换或失效 |\\\\n\\\\n合法性首先来自模型 forward 语义，而不是实现者临时选一个 mask。需要同时满足：shape 与 mask 和训练/推理契约一致；padding、无效源位置和空位置被正确屏蔽；decoder self 不泄漏未来目标 token；cross 不读取尚未提交或无权读取的源位置；batch 内不同请求的源段、目标段和页表不互相穿透；缓存 dtype、量化 scale、head 顺序和页布局与读取内核一致。\\\\n\\\\n“所有 attention 都用 causal”是结构性错误：encoder 双向、cross 可见性和 decoder 因果是三种不同函数。反过来，“cross 永远看完整源”也不成立；流式模型可能只允许当前块及 lookahead。mask 不是性能开关，改变它通常改变模型函数。\\\\n\\\\n## 源缓存复用：条件与反例\\\\n\\\\n固定源 E、固定投影权重 W^K_l、W^V_l 且可见源集合不变时，K_l、V_l 与 decoder 步数无关，可以一次生成、多次读取。若新源只是在旧源后追加位置，且模型契约保证旧位置的 E 不变、mask 只是在末尾扩展，则 cross K/V 可以追加；如果双向 encoder 因新增音频重新解释旧帧，旧位置的 E_old 改变，旧 cross K/V 就不能再当作新源的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n设源层数 L、每层 cross KV 宽度 D_kv＝H_cross·d_h、每元素 b 字节，则全部 cross K/V 约为 2LS D_kv b 字节；只存 E 约为 S d_e b 字节；目标 self KV 约为 2LT D_kv b 字节。三者不是同一对象：E 是 encoder 产物，cross K/V 是逐层投影后的只读状态，self KV 随目标生成增长。\\\\n\\\\n设定 S＝1000、d_e＝1024、L＝12、D_kv＝1024、BF16 的 b＝2，则 E 为 1000×1024×2＝2,048,000 字节，即 1.953125 MiB；全部 cross KV 为 2×12×1000×1024×2＝49,152,000 字节，即 46.875 MiB；100 条已编码请求全部提前投影约为 4.57763671875 GiB，而只保存 E 约为 195.3125 MiB。该设定说明“省掉重复投影”与“增加常驻状态”必须同时记账，不能只报告计算下降。\\\\n\\\\n反例：源 v 在旧位置改了内容或换了 processor/权重，却继续复用 v 的 cross K/V，decoder 会读到旧内容；即使新 K/V 迟到，也不能覆盖新请求的地址。缓存键至少包含源内容/版本、processor、encoder、cross 投影权重、量化/布局和可见源范围。近似复用只能声明误差范围，不能声称为逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n## 算法：源产物、解码推进与状态变化\\\\n\\\\n下面的伪代码给出一个模型契约明确的路径。它不规定某个模型必须支持任意块，而是把“何时可追加、何时必须失效”写成状态操作。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM BuildSourceState(A_visible, meta, processor, encoder, W, v)\\\\n输入：可见音频/文本、采样率与声道、processor 版本、源版本 v\\\\n输出：SourceState(v, S_valid, E, K_cross[1..L], V_cross[1..L]) 或错误\\\\n1. 校验 meta：采样率、声道、时间区间、processor 版本与请求身份一致；\\\\n2. X ← processor(A_visible)；得到特征有效位置与 padding mask；\\\\n3. E ← encoder(X, valid_mask)；只保留模型定义的有效源位置；\\\\n4. for l ← 1..L:\\\\n       K_cross[l] ← E·W_K[l]；V_cross[l] ← E·W_V[l]；\\\\n5. 返回 SourceState，并把 v、S_valid、E 与 cross K/V 绑定为同一内容身份；\\\\n6. 若源为空或有效长度为 0：返回 EMPTY_SOURCE，不进入 cross 解码。\\\\n\\\\nALGORITHM DecodeStep(req, source_state, budget)\\\\n输入：请求状态、源状态、剩余时间/长度预算\\\\n输出：新增目标 token、更新后的 self KV、提交边界或等待/失败原因\\\\n1. 若 req 已取消：返回 CANCELLED；\\\\n2. 若 source_state 的版本与 req 依赖的源版本不兼容：拒绝继续，标记需要重算或换源；\\\\n3. 初始化 t ← req.next_target_position；\\\\n4. while 未到 EOS、长度上限或预算边界:\\\\n       H_t ← decoder_forward(y_{<t}, self_KV, source_state.cross_KV,\\\\n                            M_self, M_cross, task_tokens)；\\\\n       logits ← output_head(H_t)；按任务规则选择或采样 y_t；\\\\n       更新 self_KV[t]；把 y_t 记为暂定输出；\\\\n       若 y_t 满足稳定规则：提交稳定前缀、时间戳或样本边界；\\\\n       t ← t＋1；\\\\n5. 若当前块不是最后一块：保留 source_state 与可继续的 self KV，返回 WAIT_NEXT_BLOCK；\\\\n6. 若当前块是最后一块：执行模型允许的 flush，消费最后 lookahead，提交 END_OF_REQUEST；\\\\n7. 若失败：停止新工作，按代次丢弃迟到结果；等待在途 encoder/decoder 到达可回收边界。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n状态推进可写成：WAIT_BLOCK → ENCODING → SOURCE_READY → DECODING → PUBLISHING → DONE；取消或失败进入 CANCELLED/FAILED。关键不变量是：源版本只前进不倒退；cross KV 的版本、源有效范围与内容身份一致；已提交样本偏移和稳定文本前缀不缩短；暂定文本可修订但已发布稳定文本不能被静默改写；旧代次的迟到 encoder 结果、cross 投影和解码 token 不能写入新状态。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、通信、准备与驻留\\\\n\\\\n计算上，encoder 的 self-attention 与 FFN 随源长 S 和模型宽度变化；固定 30 秒 padding 的模型会让短音频也支付较大的 encoder 固定成本，变长 encoder 则让成本随实际长度下降，但训练分布、短音频上下文和长音频外推仍限制质量。cross 投影一次约为 2LS d_e D_kv 次乘加；若每个目标步都重算源投影，则约乘以 T。缓存 cross K/V 消除了重复投影，但每步的 Q_tK_l^T、softmax 和加权求和仍然存在，约随 TS 增长。\\\\n\\\\ndecoder self-attention 每步读取长度 t 的历史；有 self KV 时每步约 O(t D_kv)，总目标计算仍约 O(T^2 D_kv)，只是避免了对历史重新做投影。访存上，cross K/V 每步都可能从 HBM 或主存取回；若每个目标步都读全部源状态，总流量约为 cross 状态字节数乘 T。E 很小而 cross K/V 很大时，保留 E、按层投影或分层换入可能比常驻全部 cross K/V 更合适。\\\\n\\\\n通信上，encoder 与 decoder 分设备时至少要传 E 或 cross K/V；源表示字节为 S d_e b，全部 cross K/V 字节为 2LS D_kv b，跨设备重复传输会改变“本地缓存是否值得”的结论。准备成本包括 resample、特征窗、tokenizer、任务 token、时间戳规则和源版本注册；这些成本不会因为 attention 很快而消失。同步成本包括 encoder 完成、块提交、投影写入和发布边界；小块增加启动次数和边界开销，大块增加首段等待。\\\\n\\\\n驻留同时包含音频环形缓冲、特征、E、各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、待发布文本和在途结果。每项都要有容量上限和所有权；平均请求小不能证明有界内存。共享页只应计一次物理字节，但每个读者仍有生命周期。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n源固定、目标很长时，cross K/V 缓存通常值得保留；源每个块都重编码且旧位置可能改变时，跨块复用旧 cross KV 不合法，应只保留 E、重投影或换用支持稳定前缀的模型。目标很短、源也很短时，一次投影与每步重算的差距可能小于额外状态和页表成本，重算反而更简单。内存紧张时，可只保留 E 或逐层构建；带宽紧张时，即使投影计算省了，若每步仍读全部 cross KV，收益也可能被传输覆盖。encoder 与 decoder 分设备时，先比较传输 E 与传输 cross KV 的字节，再决定在哪一侧投影；不能用“同一条请求”替代内容身份与布局身份。\\\\n\\\\n块大小与 lookahead 是服务目标的选择，不是模型能力的证明。更小块可能降低首段等待，却增加 processor、启动、边界和不稳定文本；更大块减少调用次数，却增加采集等待和首段延迟。batch 聚合可按音频长度或源几何做，但 decoder 应按目标迭代推进；让两个阶段共享同一个无界队列，可能让短命令排在长录音后面。\\\\n\\\\n精度、布局或页长改变后，要重新检查缓存合法性和内核契约。低位 cross KV 减少字节，但量化 scale、反量化和误差必须按模型与任务验证；E 与 cross K/V 使用不同表示时，不能用同一缓存键。\\\\n\\\\n## 流式状态机、提交链与服务目标\\\\n\\\\nASR 至少要区分：首个稳定文字延迟、整段完成延迟、实时率、词错误率 WER 和字符错误率 CER。实时率是处理耗时／音频时长，小于 1 只说明平均供给不落后，不能证明首段快；若模型等固定大窗口，计算再快也可能交互迟钝。WER 按固定文字标准化规则定义为（替换＋删除＋插入）／参考词数；CER 只对任务定义适用的语言使用。\\\\n\\\\n一次请求的提交链应保存：原始采样与声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、encoder 可见范围、任务 token、源版本、已提交样本偏移、已提交稳定文本和时间戳、暂定文本。重采样和特征窗有自己的边缘与历史；对每个网络包独立重置 processor 会破坏连续音频。发布阶段要判断某段文字是暂定还是稳定；暂定可被修订，稳定片段要有不可倒退的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n阶段队列应有界：源音频、特征、E/cross KV、decoder 状态和待发布文本分别按字节或时长限流。一个源尚未准备好不应阻塞其他就绪 decoder；一个慢客户端也不应让生成无限领先。取消时，各阶段按代次丢弃结果，已经发布的稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n## 离线切块、固定窗口与真正流式\\\\n\\\\nWhisper 的固定版本以 16 kHz 音频、80 通道 log-magnitude Mel、25 ms 窗与 10 ms 步长形成特征，按 30 秒音频块训练和推理；任务、语言、是否时间戳等通过 decoder 的条件 token 指定，时间戳相对当前音频窗口并以 20 ms 量化。长录音的 buffered transcription 会按预测时间戳移动 30 秒窗口，并可能用前文条件；这不是“任意新块都可追加 cross KV”的证明。\\\\n\\\\nMoonshine 的固定版本使用变长音频输入，不使用 Mel，而用 strides 为 64、3、2 的卷积 stem 压缩原始波形，并在 encoder/decoder 各层使用 RoPE；训练实例约在 4 到 30 秒之间。论文报告变长 encoder 可减少短音频的固定 padding 计算，并在其基准中比较了 Whisper tiny.en；同一论文也报告极短音频和超过训练长度的音频有质量限制。变长输入能力、减少 padding、真正按稳定块延续，是三件需要分别验证的能力。\\\\n\\\\n例如把一段 20 秒音频切成两个 10 秒窗口，重复上下文、时间戳偏移、说话者连续性、跨块词和拼接规则都进入输出语义。每块单独识别正确，不自动保证拼接后的全局文本和时间对齐正确；若 encoder 是双向的，新增帧还可能改变旧帧表示，先前 cross KV 就不能视为不可变前缀。\\\\n\\\\n## 场景：八路低延迟转写\\\\n\\\\n以下为设计设定，不是设备实测。八条会话输入 16 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM，每条每 200 ms 产生 3200 个样本，即 6400 字节；总输入为每秒 256000 字节。目标是在允许的文字稳定规则下，首个稳定片段于首个相关采样后 500 ms 内发布，同时在固定评测集上满足任务定义的 WER 门槛。\\\\n\\\\n候选 A 等待完整 1 秒窗口后识别；候选 B 每 200 ms 重跑当前音频窗口并允许修订暂定文字；候选 C 使用明确支持 200 ms 可提交块、100 ms lookahead 的模型执行增量处理。A 的等待下界已经超过 500 ms，不能用低实时率弥补。B 可较早展示文字，但首次猜测时间不等于稳定提交时间，且重复编码成本随窗口增长。C 的合法性依赖模型与 processor 契约，不能把这种块大小直接赋予 Whisper 或 Moonshine。\\\\n\\\\n对 C，再设排队/聚批合计 25 ms、encoder 40 ms、decoder 35 ms、发布 10 ms，则首块完成的设定时序为 200＋100＋25＋40＋35＋10＝410 ms。该和式只是所设路径，没有证明真实设备达到目标。若八路每秒各产生 5 块，总计 40 块/s，逐块 encoder＋decoder 串行占用 75 ms，则同一串行资源每秒需求 3 秒，队列必持续增长。若允许将八块聚批并把该组执行降为 110 ms，则每 200 ms 服务一组的等效占用为 55%，但实际到达相位、聚批等待和长尾仍需测量。\\\\n\\\\n容量同时包含采集环形缓冲、特征、encoder 状态、E/cross KV、目标 self KV 和待发布文本。每块应携带会话、源区间与代次；断线恢复、重复包和迟到块不能重复推进。B 的源版本变化可能使已生成目标状态失效；C 的稳定源也必须按模型要求保留 lookback。取消时各阶段共同结束，已发布稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n验证以相同原始音频和标注比较三方案，固定文字标准化规则后计算 WER；加入静音、极短指令、噪声、说话速度、跨块词和长句，分别统计最终正确性、暂定文字修订、稳定片段延迟、音频丢失、队列与实时率。不能删去错误或超时片段后再报告平均 WER/时延。若任务只要求整段录音最终结果，A 的简单批处理可能更合算；若稳定延迟严格且质量允许的原生流式模型可用，C 才有明确优势；若 B 的重复计算可接受且产品允许修订，它可能是有效中间选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释、反例与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 可控改变 | 区分与反证 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 首个稳定文字很慢 | 等待块/lookahead、排队、encoder、decoder | 只改块大小与 lookahead，保持音频和目标长度 | 若等待不变，块等待不是主因；分别记录块就绪、encoder 完成、首 token、发布 |\\\\n| 短音频仍有固定延迟 | 固定 30 秒 padding、decoder 目标长度、启动开销 | 同目标长度比较短/长音频；同源长比较目标长度 | encoder 曲线平坦而目标曲线上升，指向固定 padding；两者都平坦则查启动/排队 |\\\\n| cross 缓存没有收益 | 源每块都变、投影本来很短、每步读 cross KV 的流量主导 | 固定源开关缓存；记录投影时间、cross 读字节和 HBM 命中 | 固定源仍不降，说明瓶颈不在投影；缓存降计算但总时延升，考虑流量和驻留 |\\\\n| 流式 WER 边界变差 | 上下文短、lookahead 不足、时间戳拼接错、模型外推失败 | 固定音频只改 lookahead；固定 lookahead 只改拼接和源版本 | 若单块正确而全局错，查时间戳与跨块拼接；若 lookahead 增加才改善，查上下文 |\\\\n| 吞吐提高但尾延迟恶化 | batch 摊薄、队列增长、共享带宽、长 kernel | 扫描 batch 与准入，记录队列和首块等待 | 只看总 tokens/s 会把拒绝或更长排队算成收益；必须同时报告完成率和 SLO |\\\\n\\\\n反例和负对照应主动制造会被拒绝的情况：把 cross 误设为按目标步因果，源中未来位置被错误屏蔽；让 decoder self 看未来目标 token；在源内容改变后复用旧 cross K/V；让旧源版本的迟到结果覆盖新请求；把独立窗口结果直接拼接却不修正时间戳。正确实现应在同一固定输入、同一源版本和明确 mask 下与独立参考一致；近似数值只能声明误差范围，不能声称逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n机制检查可在 CPU 上用小矩阵验证：缓存 cross K/V 与逐步重算输出一致；空可见集合返回零输出或等待；改旧源后旧缓存与重算产生可检测差异；编辑源或旧代次提交被拒绝。性能结论仍需目标设备上的独立实验；不能把 CPU 数学检查写成 GPU 实测。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-TRANSFORMER：Attention Is All You 与流式边界\\\\n\\\\nEncoder-decoder 不是把同一套 causal attention 跑两遍，而是把源编码与目标生成分成两个有依赖的阶段：源表示支持固定复用，目标生成按自回归推进，流式输入又让源表示可能更新。本章把源表示、两套 attention、cross KV 复用条件、块边界与提交状态放在同一条数据流上。\\\\n\\\\n## 对象、函数与状态\\\\n\\\\n设一次请求含音频或文本源 A、请求身份 r、采样率、声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、模型权重版本和任务 token。processor 把 A 变成特征 X∈R^{F×d_in}，并给出有效位置与 padding；encoder 产生源表示 E∈R^{S×d_e}。这里 S 是模型的实际源位置数，不一定等于音频采样点数或网络包数。decoder 已消费的目标前缀为 y_{<t}，第 t 步隐藏状态为 H_t。\\\\n\\\\n对第 l 层 cross-attention，令 K_l＝E·W^K_l、V_l＝E·W^V_l、Q_t＝H_t·W^Q_l，则可见源集合 M_cross 下的输出为 A_{l,t}＝softmax(Q_t K_l^T／√d_h＋M_cross)·V_l。decoder self-attention 的 K/V 来自目标历史，可见集合 M_self 只允许当前位置及之前的目标位置；encoder self-attention 的可见性由模型定义，常见离线模型可在有效源内双向，但这不是所有流式模型的承诺。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态至少包含：源版本 v、源有效长度 S、E 或各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、已计算目标位置 t、已提交稳定文本前缀、已消费源样本偏移、已发布样本或时间戳边界、暂定输出和取消代次。状态要区分已计算、已验证、已发布和已回收，不能把“模型算出 token”直接当成“用户已看到稳定文字”。\\\\n\\\\n## 三类可见性与合法性\\\\n\\\\n| attention | Q 的来源 | K/V 的来源 | 典型可见性 | 状态变化 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| encoder self | encoder 当前层 | encoder 当前层 | 由模型定义，可双向或分块 | 固定源时一次算完；流式源可能重算 |\\\\n| decoder self | decoder 当前层 | 已生成目标前缀 | 通常因果，不得看未来目标 token | 每步追加，长度随目标增长 |\\\\n| cross | decoder 当前层 | encoder 源表示 | 由任务和模型定义；流式只可看已提交源或明确 lookahead | 源固定时只读，源更新时可追加、替换或失效 |\\\\n\\\\n合法性首先来自模型 forward 语义，而不是实现者临时选一个 mask。需要同时满足：shape 与 mask 和训练/推理契约一致；padding、无效源位置和空位置被正确屏蔽；decoder self 不泄漏未来目标 token；cross 不读取尚未提交或无权读取的源位置；batch 内不同请求的源段、目标段和页表不互相穿透；缓存 dtype、量化 scale、head 顺序和页布局与读取内核一致。\\\\n\\\\n“所有 attention 都用 causal”是结构性错误：encoder 双向、cross 可见性和 decoder 因果是三种不同函数。反过来，“cross 永远看完整源”也不成立；流式模型可能只允许当前块及 lookahead。mask 不是性能开关，改变它通常改变模型函数。\\\\n\\\\n## 源缓存复用：条件与反例\\\\n\\\\n固定源 E、固定投影权重 W^K_l、W^V_l 且可见源集合不变时，K_l、V_l 与 decoder 步数无关，可以一次生成、多次读取。若新源只是在旧源后追加位置，且模型契约保证旧位置的 E 不变、mask 只是在末尾扩展，则 cross K/V 可以追加；如果双向 encoder 因新增音频重新解释旧帧，旧位置的 E_old 改变，旧 cross K/V 就不能再当作新源的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n设源层数 L、每层 cross KV 宽度 D_kv＝H_cross·d_h、每元素 b 字节，则全部 cross K/V 约为 2LS D_kv b 字节；只存 E 约为 S d_e b 字节；目标 self KV 约为 2LT D_kv b 字节。三者不是同一对象：E 是 encoder 产物，cross K/V 是逐层投影后的只读状态，self KV 随目标生成增长。\\\\n\\\\n设定 S＝1000、d_e＝1024、L＝12、D_kv＝1024、BF16 的 b＝2，则 E 为 1000×1024×2＝2,048,000 字节，即 1.953125 MiB；全部 cross KV 为 2×12×1000×1024×2＝49,152,000 字节，即 46.875 MiB；100 条已编码请求全部提前投影约为 4.57763671875 GiB，而只保存 E 约为 195.3125 MiB。该设定说明“省掉重复投影”与“增加常驻状态”必须同时记账，不能只报告计算下降。\\\\n\\\\n反例：源 v 在旧位置改了内容或换了 processor/权重，却继续复用 v 的 cross K/V，decoder 会读到旧内容；即使新 K/V 迟到，也不能覆盖新请求的地址。缓存键至少包含源内容/版本、processor、encoder、cross 投影权重、量化/布局和可见源范围。近似复用只能声明误差范围，不能声称为逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n## 算法：源产物、解码推进与状态变化\\\\n\\\\n下面的伪代码给出一个模型契约明确的路径。它不规定某个模型必须支持任意块，而是把“何时可追加、何时必须失效”写成状态操作。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM BuildSourceState(A_visible, meta, processor, encoder, W, v)\\\\n输入：可见音频/文本、采样率与声道、processor 版本、源版本 v\\\\n输出：SourceState(v, S_valid, E, K_cross[1..L], V_cross[1..L]) 或错误\\\\n1. 校验 meta：采样率、声道、时间区间、processor 版本与请求身份一致；\\\\n2. X ← processor(A_visible)；得到特征有效位置与 padding mask；\\\\n3. E ← encoder(X, valid_mask)；只保留模型定义的有效源位置；\\\\n4. for l ← 1..L:\\\\n       K_cross[l] ← E·W_K[l]；V_cross[l] ← E·W_V[l]；\\\\n5. 返回 SourceState，并把 v、S_valid、E 与 cross K/V 绑定为同一内容身份；\\\\n6. 若源为空或有效长度为 0：返回 EMPTY_SOURCE，不进入 cross 解码。\\\\n\\\\nALGORITHM DecodeStep(req, source_state, budget)\\\\n输入：请求状态、源状态、剩余时间/长度预算\\\\n输出：新增目标 token、更新后的 self KV、提交边界或等待/失败原因\\\\n1. 若 req 已取消：返回 CANCELLED；\\\\n2. 若 source_state 的版本与 req 依赖的源版本不兼容：拒绝继续，标记需要重算或换源；\\\\n3. 初始化 t ← req.next_target_position；\\\\n4. while 未到 EOS、长度上限或预算边界:\\\\n       H_t ← decoder_forward(y_{<t}, self_KV, source_state.cross_KV,\\\\n                            M_self, M_cross, task_tokens)；\\\\n       logits ← output_head(H_t)；按任务规则选择或采样 y_t；\\\\n       更新 self_KV[t]；把 y_t 记为暂定输出；\\\\n       若 y_t 满足稳定规则：提交稳定前缀、时间戳或样本边界；\\\\n       t ← t＋1；\\\\n5. 若当前块不是最后一块：保留 source_state 与可继续的 self KV，返回 WAIT_NEXT_BLOCK；\\\\n6. 若当前块是最后一块：执行模型允许的 flush，消费最后 lookahead，提交 END_OF_REQUEST；\\\\n7. 若失败：停止新工作，按代次丢弃迟到结果；等待在途 encoder/decoder 到达可回收边界。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n状态推进可写成：WAIT_BLOCK → ENCODING → SOURCE_READY → DECODING → PUBLISHING → DONE；取消或失败进入 CANCELLED/FAILED。关键不变量是：源版本只前进不倒退；cross KV 的版本、源有效范围与内容身份一致；已提交样本偏移和稳定文本前缀不缩短；暂定文本可修订但已发布稳定文本不能被静默改写；旧代次的迟到 encoder 结果、cross 投影和解码 token 不能写入新状态。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、通信、准备与驻留\\\\n\\\\n计算上，encoder 的 self-attention 与 FFN 随源长 S 和模型宽度变化；固定 30 秒 padding 的模型会让短音频也支付较大的 encoder 固定成本，变长 encoder 则让成本随实际长度下降，但训练分布、短音频上下文和长音频外推仍限制质量。cross 投影一次约为 2LS d_e D_kv 次乘加；若每个目标步都重算源投影，则约乘以 T。缓存 cross K/V 消除了重复投影，但每步的 Q_tK_l^T、softmax 和加权求和仍然存在，约随 TS 增长。\\\\n\\\\ndecoder self-attention 每步读取长度 t 的历史；有 self KV 时每步约 O(t D_kv)，总目标计算仍约 O(T^2 D_kv)，只是避免了对历史重新做投影。访存上，cross K/V 每步都可能从 HBM 或主存取回；若每个目标步都读全部源状态，总流量约为 cross 状态字节数乘 T。E 很小而 cross K/V 很大时，保留 E、按层投影或分层换入可能比常驻全部 cross K/V 更合适。\\\\n\\\\n通信上，encoder 与 decoder 分设备时至少要传 E 或 cross K/V；源表示字节为 S d_e b，全部 cross K/V 字节为 2LS D_kv b，跨设备重复传输会改变“本地缓存是否值得”的结论。准备成本包括 resample、特征窗、tokenizer、任务 token、时间戳规则和源版本注册；这些成本不会因为 attention 很快而消失。同步成本包括 encoder 完成、块提交、投影写入和发布边界；小块增加启动次数和边界开销，大块增加首段等待。\\\\n\\\\n驻留同时包含音频环形缓冲、特征、E、各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、待发布文本和在途结果。每项都要有容量上限和所有权；平均请求小不能证明有界内存。共享页只应计一次物理字节，但每个读者仍有生命周期。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n源固定、目标很长时，cross K/V 缓存通常值得保留；源每个块都重编码且旧位置可能改变时，跨块复用旧 cross KV 不合法，应只保留 E、重投影或换用支持稳定前缀的模型。目标很短、源也很短时，一次投影与每步重算的差距可能小于额外状态和页表成本，重算反而更简单。内存紧张时，可只保留 E 或逐层构建；带宽紧张时，即使投影计算省了，若每步仍读全部 cross KV，收益也可能被传输覆盖。encoder 与 decoder 分设备时，先比较传输 E 与传输 cross KV 的字节，再决定在哪一侧投影；不能用“同一条请求”替代内容身份与布局身份。\\\\n\\\\n块大小与 lookahead 是服务目标的选择，不是模型能力的证明。更小块可能降低首段等待，却增加 processor、启动、边界和不稳定文本；更大块减少调用次数，却增加采集等待和首段延迟。batch 聚合可按音频长度或源几何做，但 decoder 应按目标迭代推进；让两个阶段共享同一个无界队列，可能让短命令排在长录音后面。\\\\n\\\\n精度、布局或页长改变后，要重新检查缓存合法性和内核契约。低位 cross KV 减少字节，但量化 scale、反量化和误差必须按模型与任务验证；E 与 cross K/V 使用不同表示时，不能用同一缓存键。\\\\n\\\\n## 流式状态机、提交链与服务目标\\\\n\\\\nASR 至少要区分：首个稳定文字延迟、整段完成延迟、实时率、词错误率 WER 和字符错误率 CER。实时率是处理耗时／音频时长，小于 1 只说明平均供给不落后，不能证明首段快；若模型等固定大窗口，计算再快也可能交互迟钝。WER 按固定文字标准化规则定义为（替换＋删除＋插入）／参考词数；CER 只对任务定义适用的语言使用。\\\\n\\\\n一次请求的提交链应保存：原始采样与声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、encoder 可见范围、任务 token、源版本、已提交样本偏移、已提交稳定文本和时间戳、暂定文本。重采样和特征窗有自己的边缘与历史；对每个网络包独立重置 processor 会破坏连续音频。发布阶段要判断某段文字是暂定还是稳定；暂定可被修订，稳定片段要有不可倒退的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n阶段队列应有界：源音频、特征、E/cross KV、decoder 状态和待发布文本分别按字节或时长限流。一个源尚未准备好不应阻塞其他就绪 decoder；一个慢客户端也不应让生成无限领先。取消时，各阶段按代次丢弃结果，已经发布的稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n## 离线切块、固定窗口与真正流式\\\\n\\\\nWhisper 的固定版本以 16 kHz 音频、80 通道 log-magnitude Mel、25 ms 窗与 10 ms 步长形成特征，按 30 秒音频块训练和推理；任务、语言、是否时间戳等通过 decoder 的条件 token 指定，时间戳相对当前音频窗口并以 20 ms 量化。长录音的 buffered transcription 会按预测时间戳移动 30 秒窗口，并可能用前文条件；这不是“任意新块都可追加 cross KV”的证明。\\\\n\\\\nMoonshine 的固定版本使用变长音频输入，不使用 Mel，而用 strides 为 64、3、2 的卷积 stem 压缩原始波形，并在 encoder/decoder 各层使用 RoPE；训练实例约在 4 到 30 秒之间。论文报告变长 encoder 可减少短音频的固定 padding 计算，并在其基准中比较了 Whisper tiny.en；同一论文也报告极短音频和超过训练长度的音频有质量限制。变长输入能力、减少 padding、真正按稳定块延续，是三件需要分别验证的能力。\\\\n\\\\n例如把一段 20 秒音频切成两个 10 秒窗口，重复上下文、时间戳偏移、说话者连续性、跨块词和拼接规则都进入输出语义。每块单独识别正确，不自动保证拼接后的全局文本和时间对齐正确；若 encoder 是双向的，新增帧还可能改变旧帧表示，先前 cross KV 就不能视为不可变前缀。\\\\n\\\\n## 场景：八路低延迟转写\\\\n\\\\n以下为设计设定，不是设备实测。八条会话输入 16 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM，每条每 200 ms 产生 3200 个样本，即 6400 字节；总输入为每秒 256000 字节。目标是在允许的文字稳定规则下，首个稳定片段于首个相关采样后 500 ms 内发布，同时在固定评测集上满足任务定义的 WER 门槛。\\\\n\\\\n候选 A 等待完整 1 秒窗口后识别；候选 B 每 200 ms 重跑当前音频窗口并允许修订暂定文字；候选 C 使用明确支持 200 ms 可提交块、100 ms lookahead 的模型执行增量处理。A 的等待下界已经超过 500 ms，不能用低实时率弥补。B 可较早展示文字，但首次猜测时间不等于稳定提交时间，且重复编码成本随窗口增长。C 的合法性依赖模型与 processor 契约，不能把这种块大小直接赋予 Whisper 或 Moonshine。\\\\n\\\\n对 C，再设排队/聚批合计 25 ms、encoder 40 ms、decoder 35 ms、发布 10 ms，则首块完成的设定时序为 200＋100＋25＋40＋35＋10＝410 ms。该和式只是所设路径，没有证明真实设备达到目标。若八路每秒各产生 5 块，总计 40 块/s，逐块 encoder＋decoder 串行占用 75 ms，则同一串行资源每秒需求 3 秒，队列必持续增长。若允许将八块聚批并把该组执行降为 110 ms，则每 200 ms 服务一组的等效占用为 55%，但实际到达相位、聚批等待和长尾仍需测量。\\\\n\\\\n容量同时包含采集环形缓冲、特征、encoder 状态、E/cross KV、目标 self KV 和待发布文本。每块应携带会话、源区间与代次；断线恢复、重复包和迟到块不能重复推进。B 的源版本变化可能使已生成目标状态失效；C 的稳定源也必须按模型要求保留 lookback。取消时各阶段共同结束，已发布稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n验证以相同原始音频和标注比较三方案，固定文字标准化规则后计算 WER；加入静音、极短指令、噪声、说话速度、跨块词和长句，分别统计最终正确性、暂定文字修订、稳定片段延迟、音频丢失、队列与实时率。不能删去错误或超时片段后再报告平均 WER/时延。若任务只要求整段录音最终结果，A 的简单批处理可能更合算；若稳定延迟严格且质量允许的原生流式模型可用，C 才有明确优势；若 B 的重复计算可接受且产品允许修订，它可能是有效中间选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释、反例与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 可控改变 | 区分与反证 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 首个稳定文字很慢 | 等待块/lookahead、排队、encoder、decoder | 只改块大小与 lookahead，保持音频和目标长度 | 若等待不变，块等待不是主因；分别记录块就绪、encoder 完成、首 token、发布 |\\\\n| 短音频仍有固定延迟 | 固定 30 秒 padding、decoder 目标长度、启动开销 | 同目标长度比较短/长音频；同源长比较目标长度 | encoder 曲线平坦而目标曲线上升，指向固定 padding；两者都平坦则查启动/排队 |\\\\n| cross 缓存没有收益 | 源每块都变、投影本来很短、每步读 cross KV 的流量主导 | 固定源开关缓存；记录投影时间、cross 读字节和 HBM 命中 | 固定源仍不降，说明瓶颈不在投影；缓存降计算但总时延升，考虑流量和驻留 |\\\\n| 流式 WER 边界变差 | 上下文短、lookahead 不足、时间戳拼接错、模型外推失败 | 固定音频只改 lookahead；固定 lookahead 只改拼接和源版本 | 若单块正确而全局错，查时间戳与跨块拼接；若 lookahead 增加才改善，查上下文 |\\\\n| 吞吐提高但尾延迟恶化 | batch 摊薄、队列增长、共享带宽、长 kernel | 扫描 batch 与准入，记录队列和首块等待 | 只看总 tokens/s 会把拒绝或更长排队算成收益；必须同时报告完成率和 SLO |\\\\n\\\\n反例和负对照应主动制造会被拒绝的情况：把 cross 误设为按目标步因果，源中未来位置被错误屏蔽；让 decoder self 看未来目标 token；在源内容改变后复用旧 cross K/V；让旧源版本的迟到结果覆盖新请求；把独立窗口结果直接拼接却不修正时间戳。正确实现应在同一固定输入、同一源版本和明确 mask 下与独立参考一致；近似数值只能声明误差范围，不能声称逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n机制检查可在 CPU 上用小矩阵验证：缓存 cross K/V 与逐步重算输出一致；空可见集合返回零输出或等待；改旧源后旧缓存与重算产生可检测差异；编辑源或旧代次提交被拒绝。性能结论仍需目标设备上的独立实验；不能把 CPU 数学检查写成 GPU 实测。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-TRANSFORMER：Attention Is All You 与流式边界\\\\n\\\\nEncoder-decoder 不是把同一套 causal attention 跑两遍，而是把源编码与目标生成分成两个有依赖的阶段：源表示支持固定复用，目标生成按自回归推进，流式输入又让源表示可能更新。本章把源表示、两套 attention、cross KV 复用条件、块边界与提交状态放在同一条数据流上。\\\\n\\\\n## 对象、函数与状态\\\\n\\\\n设一次请求含音频或文本源 A、请求身份 r、采样率、声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、模型权重版本和任务 token。processor 把 A 变成特征 X∈R^{F×d_in}，并给出有效位置与 padding；encoder 产生源表示 E∈R^{S×d_e}。这里 S 是模型的实际源位置数，不一定等于音频采样点数或网络包数。decoder 已消费的目标前缀为 y_{<t}，第 t 步隐藏状态为 H_t。\\\\n\\\\n对第 l 层 cross-attention，令 K_l＝E·W^K_l、V_l＝E·W^V_l、Q_t＝H_t·W^Q_l，则可见源集合 M_cross 下的输出为 A_{l,t}＝softmax(Q_t K_l^T／√d_h＋M_cross)·V_l。decoder self-attention 的 K/V 来自目标历史，可见集合 M_self 只允许当前位置及之前的目标位置；encoder self-attention 的可见性由模型定义，常见离线模型可在有效源内双向，但这不是所有流式模型的承诺。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态至少包含：源版本 v、源有效长度 S、E 或各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、已计算目标位置 t、已提交稳定文本前缀、已消费源样本偏移、已发布样本或时间戳边界、暂定输出和取消代次。状态要区分已计算、已验证、已发布和已回收，不能把“模型算出 token”直接当成“用户已看到稳定文字”。\\\\n\\\\n## 三类可见性与合法性\\\\n\\\\n| attention | Q 的来源 | K/V 的来源 | 典型可见性 | 状态变化 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| encoder self | encoder 当前层 | encoder 当前层 | 由模型定义，可双向或分块 | 固定源时一次算完；流式源可能重算 |\\\\n| decoder self | decoder 当前层 | 已生成目标前缀 | 通常因果，不得看未来目标 token | 每步追加，长度随目标增长 |\\\\n| cross | decoder 当前层 | encoder 源表示 | 由任务和模型定义；流式只可看已提交源或明确 lookahead | 源固定时只读，源更新时可追加、替换或失效 |\\\\n\\\\n合法性首先来自模型 forward 语义，而不是实现者临时选一个 mask。需要同时满足：shape 与 mask 和训练/推理契约一致；padding、无效源位置和空位置被正确屏蔽；decoder self 不泄漏未来目标 token；cross 不读取尚未提交或无权读取的源位置；batch 内不同请求的源段、目标段和页表不互相穿透；缓存 dtype、量化 scale、head 顺序和页布局与读取内核一致。\\\\n\\\\n“所有 attention 都用 causal”是结构性错误：encoder 双向、cross 可见性和 decoder 因果是三种不同函数。反过来，“cross 永远看完整源”也不成立；流式模型可能只允许当前块及 lookahead。mask 不是性能开关，改变它通常改变模型函数。\\\\n\\\\n## 源缓存复用：条件与反例\\\\n\\\\n固定源 E、固定投影权重 W^K_l、W^V_l 且可见源集合不变时，K_l、V_l 与 decoder 步数无关，可以一次生成、多次读取。若新源只是在旧源后追加位置，且模型契约保证旧位置的 E 不变、mask 只是在末尾扩展，则 cross K/V 可以追加；如果双向 encoder 因新增音频重新解释旧帧，旧位置的 E_old 改变，旧 cross K/V 就不能再当作新源的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n设源层数 L、每层 cross KV 宽度 D_kv＝H_cross·d_h、每元素 b 字节，则全部 cross K/V 约为 2LS D_kv b 字节；只存 E 约为 S d_e b 字节；目标 self KV 约为 2LT D_kv b 字节。三者不是同一对象：E 是 encoder 产物，cross K/V 是逐层投影后的只读状态，self KV 随目标生成增长。\\\\n\\\\n设定 S＝1000、d_e＝1024、L＝12、D_kv＝1024、BF16 的 b＝2，则 E 为 1000×1024×2＝2,048,000 字节，即 1.953125 MiB；全部 cross KV 为 2×12×1000×1024×2＝49,152,000 字节，即 46.875 MiB；100 条已编码请求全部提前投影约为 4.57763671875 GiB，而只保存 E 约为 195.3125 MiB。该设定说明“省掉重复投影”与“增加常驻状态”必须同时记账，不能只报告计算下降。\\\\n\\\\n反例：源 v 在旧位置改了内容或换了 processor/权重，却继续复用 v 的 cross K/V，decoder 会读到旧内容；即使新 K/V 迟到，也不能覆盖新请求的地址。缓存键至少包含源内容/版本、processor、encoder、cross 投影权重、量化/布局和可见源范围。近似复用只能声明误差范围，不能声称为逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n## 算法：源产物、解码推进与状态变化\\\\n\\\\n下面的伪代码给出一个模型契约明确的路径。它不规定某个模型必须支持任意块，而是把“何时可追加、何时必须失效”写成状态操作。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nALGORITHM BuildSourceState(A_visible, meta, processor, encoder, W, v)\\\\n输入：可见音频/文本、采样率与声道、processor 版本、源版本 v\\\\n输出：SourceState(v, S_valid, E, K_cross[1..L], V_cross[1..L]) 或错误\\\\n1. 校验 meta：采样率、声道、时间区间、processor 版本与请求身份一致；\\\\n2. X ← processor(A_visible)；得到特征有效位置与 padding mask；\\\\n3. E ← encoder(X, valid_mask)；只保留模型定义的有效源位置；\\\\n4. for l ← 1..L:\\\\n       K_cross[l] ← E·W_K[l]；V_cross[l] ← E·W_V[l]；\\\\n5. 返回 SourceState，并把 v、S_valid、E 与 cross K/V 绑定为同一内容身份；\\\\n6. 若源为空或有效长度为 0：返回 EMPTY_SOURCE，不进入 cross 解码。\\\\n\\\\nALGORITHM DecodeStep(req, source_state, budget)\\\\n输入：请求状态、源状态、剩余时间/长度预算\\\\n输出：新增目标 token、更新后的 self KV、提交边界或等待/失败原因\\\\n1. 若 req 已取消：返回 CANCELLED；\\\\n2. 若 source_state 的版本与 req 依赖的源版本不兼容：拒绝继续，标记需要重算或换源；\\\\n3. 初始化 t ← req.next_target_position；\\\\n4. while 未到 EOS、长度上限或预算边界:\\\\n       H_t ← decoder_forward(y_{<t}, self_KV, source_state.cross_KV,\\\\n                            M_self, M_cross, task_tokens)；\\\\n       logits ← output_head(H_t)；按任务规则选择或采样 y_t；\\\\n       更新 self_KV[t]；把 y_t 记为暂定输出；\\\\n       若 y_t 满足稳定规则：提交稳定前缀、时间戳或样本边界；\\\\n       t ← t＋1；\\\\n5. 若当前块不是最后一块：保留 source_state 与可继续的 self KV，返回 WAIT_NEXT_BLOCK；\\\\n6. 若当前块是最后一块：执行模型允许的 flush，消费最后 lookahead，提交 END_OF_REQUEST；\\\\n7. 若失败：停止新工作，按代次丢弃迟到结果；等待在途 encoder/decoder 到达可回收边界。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n状态推进可写成：WAIT_BLOCK → ENCODING → SOURCE_READY → DECODING → PUBLISHING → DONE；取消或失败进入 CANCELLED/FAILED。关键不变量是：源版本只前进不倒退；cross KV 的版本、源有效范围与内容身份一致；已提交样本偏移和稳定文本前缀不缩短；暂定文本可修订但已发布稳定文本不能被静默改写；旧代次的迟到 encoder 结果、cross 投影和解码 token 不能写入新状态。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、通信、准备与驻留\\\\n\\\\n计算上，encoder 的 self-attention 与 FFN 随源长 S 和模型宽度变化；固定 30 秒 padding 的模型会让短音频也支付较大的 encoder 固定成本，变长 encoder 则让成本随实际长度下降，但训练分布、短音频上下文和长音频外推仍限制质量。cross 投影一次约为 2LS d_e D_kv 次乘加；若每个目标步都重算源投影，则约乘以 T。缓存 cross K/V 消除了重复投影，但每步的 Q_tK_l^T、softmax 和加权求和仍然存在，约随 TS 增长。\\\\n\\\\ndecoder self-attention 每步读取长度 t 的历史；有 self KV 时每步约 O(t D_kv)，总目标计算仍约 O(T^2 D_kv)，只是避免了对历史重新做投影。访存上，cross K/V 每步都可能从 HBM 或主存取回；若每个目标步都读全部源状态，总流量约为 cross 状态字节数乘 T。E 很小而 cross K/V 很大时，保留 E、按层投影或分层换入可能比常驻全部 cross K/V 更合适。\\\\n\\\\n通信上，encoder 与 decoder 分设备时至少要传 E 或 cross K/V；源表示字节为 S d_e b，全部 cross K/V 字节为 2LS D_kv b，跨设备重复传输会改变“本地缓存是否值得”的结论。准备成本包括 resample、特征窗、tokenizer、任务 token、时间戳规则和源版本注册；这些成本不会因为 attention 很快而消失。同步成本包括 encoder 完成、块提交、投影写入和发布边界；小块增加启动次数和边界开销，大块增加首段等待。\\\\n\\\\n驻留同时包含音频环形缓冲、特征、E、各层 cross K/V、目标 self KV、待发布文本和在途结果。每项都要有容量上限和所有权；平均请求小不能证明有界内存。共享页只应计一次物理字节，但每个读者仍有生命周期。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n源固定、目标很长时，cross K/V 缓存通常值得保留；源每个块都重编码且旧位置可能改变时，跨块复用旧 cross KV 不合法，应只保留 E、重投影或换用支持稳定前缀的模型。目标很短、源也很短时，一次投影与每步重算的差距可能小于额外状态和页表成本，重算反而更简单。内存紧张时，可只保留 E 或逐层构建；带宽紧张时，即使投影计算省了，若每步仍读全部 cross KV，收益也可能被传输覆盖。encoder 与 decoder 分设备时，先比较传输 E 与传输 cross KV 的字节，再决定在哪一侧投影；不能用“同一条请求”替代内容身份与布局身份。\\\\n\\\\n块大小与 lookahead 是服务目标的选择，不是模型能力的证明。更小块可能降低首段等待，却增加 processor、启动、边界和不稳定文本；更大块减少调用次数，却增加采集等待和首段延迟。batch 聚合可按音频长度或源几何做，但 decoder 应按目标迭代推进；让两个阶段共享同一个无界队列，可能让短命令排在长录音后面。\\\\n\\\\n精度、布局或页长改变后，要重新检查缓存合法性和内核契约。低位 cross KV 减少字节，但量化 scale、反量化和误差必须按模型与任务验证；E 与 cross K/V 使用不同表示时，不能用同一缓存键。\\\\n\\\\n## 流式状态机、提交链与服务目标\\\\n\\\\nASR 至少要区分：首个稳定文字延迟、整段完成延迟、实时率、词错误率 WER 和字符错误率 CER。实时率是处理耗时／音频时长，小于 1 只说明平均供给不落后，不能证明首段快；若模型等固定大窗口，计算再快也可能交互迟钝。WER 按固定文字标准化规则定义为（替换＋删除＋插入）／参考词数；CER 只对任务定义适用的语言使用。\\\\n\\\\n一次请求的提交链应保存：原始采样与声道、源时间区间、processor 版本、encoder 可见范围、任务 token、源版本、已提交样本偏移、已提交稳定文本和时间戳、暂定文本。重采样和特征窗有自己的边缘与历史；对每个网络包独立重置 processor 会破坏连续音频。发布阶段要判断某段文字是暂定还是稳定；暂定可被修订，稳定片段要有不可倒退的前缀。\\\\n\\\\n阶段队列应有界：源音频、特征、E/cross KV、decoder 状态和待发布文本分别按字节或时长限流。一个源尚未准备好不应阻塞其他就绪 decoder；一个慢客户端也不应让生成无限领先。取消时，各阶段按代次丢弃结果，已经发布的稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n## 离线切块、固定窗口与真正流式\\\\n\\\\nWhisper 的固定版本以 16 kHz 音频、80 通道 log-magnitude Mel、25 ms 窗与 10 ms 步长形成特征，按 30 秒音频块训练和推理；任务、语言、是否时间戳等通过 decoder 的条件 token 指定，时间戳相对当前音频窗口并以 20 ms 量化。长录音的 buffered transcription 会按预测时间戳移动 30 秒窗口，并可能用前文条件；这不是“任意新块都可追加 cross KV”的证明。\\\\n\\\\nMoonshine 的固定版本使用变长音频输入，不使用 Mel，而用 strides 为 64、3、2 的卷积 stem 压缩原始波形，并在 encoder/decoder 各层使用 RoPE；训练实例约在 4 到 30 秒之间。论文报告变长 encoder 可减少短音频的固定 padding 计算，并在其基准中比较了 Whisper tiny.en；同一论文也报告极短音频和超过训练长度的音频有质量限制。变长输入能力、减少 padding、真正按稳定块延续，是三件需要分别验证的能力。\\\\n\\\\n例如把一段 20 秒音频切成两个 10 秒窗口，重复上下文、时间戳偏移、说话者连续性、跨块词和拼接规则都进入输出语义。每块单独识别正确，不自动保证拼接后的全局文本和时间对齐正确；若 encoder 是双向的，新增帧还可能改变旧帧表示，先前 cross KV 就不能视为不可变前缀。\\\\n\\\\n## 场景：八路低延迟转写\\\\n\\\\n以下为设计设定，不是设备实测。八条会话输入 16 kHz、单声道、16-bit PCM，每条每 200 ms 产生 3200 个样本，即 6400 字节；总输入为每秒 256000 字节。目标是在允许的文字稳定规则下，首个稳定片段于首个相关采样后 500 ms 内发布，同时在固定评测集上满足任务定义的 WER 门槛。\\\\n\\\\n候选 A 等待完整 1 秒窗口后识别；候选 B 每 200 ms 重跑当前音频窗口并允许修订暂定文字；候选 C 使用明确支持 200 ms 可提交块、100 ms lookahead 的模型执行增量处理。A 的等待下界已经超过 500 ms，不能用低实时率弥补。B 可较早展示文字，但首次猜测时间不等于稳定提交时间，且重复编码成本随窗口增长。C 的合法性依赖模型与 processor 契约，不能把这种块大小直接赋予 Whisper 或 Moonshine。\\\\n\\\\n对 C，再设排队/聚批合计 25 ms、encoder 40 ms、decoder 35 ms、发布 10 ms，则首块完成的设定时序为 200＋100＋25＋40＋35＋10＝410 ms。该和式只是所设路径，没有证明真实设备达到目标。若八路每秒各产生 5 块，总计 40 块/s，逐块 encoder＋decoder 串行占用 75 ms，则同一串行资源每秒需求 3 秒，队列必持续增长。若允许将八块聚批并把该组执行降为 110 ms，则每 200 ms 服务一组的等效占用为 55%，但实际到达相位、聚批等待和长尾仍需测量。\\\\n\\\\n容量同时包含采集环形缓冲、特征、encoder 状态、E/cross KV、目标 self KV 和待发布文本。每块应携带会话、源区间与代次；断线恢复、重复包和迟到块不能重复推进。B 的源版本变化可能使已生成目标状态失效；C 的稳定源也必须按模型要求保留 lookback。取消时各阶段共同结束，已发布稳定文本保留明确终态。\\\\n\\\\n验证以相同原始音频和标注比较三方案，固定文字标准化规则后计算 WER；加入静音、极短指令、噪声、说话速度、跨块词和长句，分别统计最终正确性、暂定文字修订、稳定片段延迟、音频丢失、队列与实时率。不能删去错误或超时片段后再报告平均 WER/时延。若任务只要求整段录音最终结果，A 的简单批处理可能更合算；若稳定延迟严格且质量允许的原生流式模型可用，C 才有明确优势；若 B 的重复计算可接受且产品允许修订，它可能是有效中间选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释、反例与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 可控改变 | 区分与反证 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 首个稳定文字很慢 | 等待块/lookahead、排队、encoder、decoder | 只改块大小与 lookahead，保持音频和目标长度 | 若等待不变，块等待不是主因；分别记录块就绪、encoder 完成、首 token、发布 |\\\\n| 短音频仍有固定延迟 | 固定 30 秒 padding、decoder 目标长度、启动开销 | 同目标长度比较短/长音频；同源长比较目标长度 | encoder 曲线平坦而目标曲线上升，指向固定 padding；两者都平坦则查启动/排队 |\\\\n| cross 缓存没有收益 | 源每块都变、投影本来很短、每步读 cross KV 的流量主导 | 固定源开关缓存；记录投影时间、cross 读字节和 HBM 命中 | 固定源仍不降，说明瓶颈不在投影；缓存降计算但总时延升，考虑流量和驻留 |\\\\n| 流式 WER 边界变差 | 上下文短、lookahead 不足、时间戳拼接错、模型外推失败 | 固定音频只改 lookahead；固定 lookahead 只改拼接和源版本 | 若单块正确而全局错，查时间戳与跨块拼接；若 lookahead 增加才改善，查上下文 |\\\\n| 吞吐提高但尾延迟恶化 | batch 摊薄、队列增长、共享带宽、长 kernel | 扫描 batch 与准入，记录队列和首块等待 | 只看总 tokens/s 会把拒绝或更长排队算成收益；必须同时报告完成率和 SLO |\\\\n\\\\n反例和负对照应主动制造会被拒绝的情况：把 cross 误设为按目标步因果，源中未来位置被错误屏蔽；让 decoder self 看未来目标 token；在源内容改变后复用旧 cross K/V；让旧源版本的迟到结果覆盖新请求；把独立窗口结果直接拼接却不修正时间戳。正确实现应在同一固定输入、同一源版本和明确 mask 下与独立参考一致；近似数值只能声明误差范围，不能声称逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n机制检查可在 CPU 上用小矩阵验证：缓存 cross K/V 与逐步重算输出一致；空可见集合返回零输出或等待；改旧源后旧缓存与重算产生可检测差异；编辑源或旧代次提交被拒绝。性能结论仍需目标设备上的独立实验；不能把 CPU 数学检查写成 GPU 实测。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-TRANSFORMER：Attention Is All You 正文与算法\\\\n\\\\n正文以问题和机制展开：说明问题为什么出现，定义对象和合法性，展开算法、数据流与状态更新，推导成本与组合关系，用设定算例、反例和区分实验解释结论如何改变。篇幅与结构由内容决定，不规定候选数、反例数或统一段落数量。\\\\n\\\\n实现逻辑可以转写为完整的算法伪代码，使用 pseudocode kernel、项目类结构、注册器、兼容分支和可执行命令保留在工程中。\\\\n\\\\n公式须说明符号、单位、轴和假设。区分逻辑数据量、实际设备事务量、容量峰值和关键路径时间；重叠工作不能把全部耗时直接相加。模型结构、数值策略、硬件能力或运行规模改变后，重新检查依赖与成本。\\\\n\\\\n## 来源阅读链\\\\n\\\\n论文保留直接可读的原始 PDF、必要图片和出处；来源说明用自己的话展开算法、推导、论文结论及其条件，明确哪些是论文报告、哪些是本库计算。文档同样保留原文，提炼定义、语义、约束及其设计含义。\\\\n\\\\n源码可以供知识编写者核对机制。交给 Agent 的内容应是经过核对的算法伪代码、数据流、状态关系与条件化事实，不能把整个实现文件称作知识原文。文档/源码混合资料按实际内容选择可读文档；文件扩展名、压缩包形式和仓库名称本身不决定知识价值。已有源码归档可以保留供溯源审计，其字节和哈希不因来源说明修订而改变。\\\\n\\\\n正文引用需要带实质内容，再指向来源说明；来源说明指向可读论文或文档。必要内容离线可读，不依赖 Agent 联网补全。准确版本留作证据身份；只有影响本题合法性或成本的版本事实进入论证，不搬运与本题无关的参数和分支。\\\\n\\\\n## 逐层阅读\\\\n\\\\n阅读入口按主题地图、章节摘要与问题/前提、二级节结构、完整论证、来源原文展开。Agent 自主选择阅读深度；索引与检索结果提供相邻机制，不产生必读清单。读取按实际字符范围与冻结修订记录；读过摘要不等于读过整章。\\\\n\\\\n## Base、观测和 workflow\\\\n\\\\nBase 的来源事实受发布版本的时间上限约束；编辑日期不改变事实日期。新的整理和独立推导保留真实日期与依据，后续实验不能伪装成历史 seed。\\\\n\\\\n运行观测保存环境、workload、测量方法、数值/单位/不确定性、实验证据与真实日期。机制知识解释因果、条件、预测和反例。Workflow 保存一类局部设计、诊断或验证问题的触发条件、前提、步骤、检查与退出/调整条件、成本和复用边界。三者相互引用，不能用一次成功代替机制解释或跨条件验证。\\\\n\\\\nEvolution 提炼、Diagnostician 独立复核，沿已有发布和证据机制进入后续冻结、检索与读取。Workflow 为可选方法，不自动成为 Controller 的全局顺序。跨任务资格使用现有权威晋升机制，负面与不确定结果保留，不建立平行资格体系。\\\\n\\\\n## 修订、覆盖和验证\\\\n\\\\n已有技术对象优先深化原章；独立对象才新增章节。修订保存登记前正文与元数据的准确字节，更新 catalog、来源说明哈希、导航、时间审计、VERSION 与变更清单。已存在的来源归档保持原身份。\\\\n\\\\n覆盖审计同时检查能力域、具体算法与跨机制组合，区分完整解释、仅提及、缺少推导、缺少证据和缺失；篇数和术语命中不是覆盖证明。结构/身份检查、独立算法算例、运行时读取/发布测试与真实构建效果分别报告。通过前几项不能声称已证明知识改善了 Agent
